### Constitutional Rule Catalogue

The rules below are the complete constitutional rule set for CAT planning as of this version. They are numbered `CAT-PE-CONST-001` upward and are cited by identifier everywhere else in this part. This is the full set, not a sample: a planning behaviour not governed by one of these rules is governed by the section that describes it, and a conflict between a section and a rule is resolved in favour of the rule.

| Rule ID | Title | Enforcement point | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CAT-PE-CONST-001` | Intent precedes derivation | Intent admission gate at the entry of the derivation core. | Planning Owner Council |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-002` | Every derived object names its parent | Reference resolution at the repository contract layer on every write. | Planning Data Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-003` | Goals are outcomes, not activities | Goal admission review with a structural check for activity verbs and deliverable nouns. | Goal Portfolio Owner |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-004` | Objectives are measurable or they are not objectives | Objective activation gate in the objective core. | Objective Steward |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-005` | Baselines are frozen before measurement | Baseline freeze at objective activation, enforced by the immutability of the activated version. | Objective Steward |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-006` | Tasks declare a definition of done | Readiness gate in the task core, evaluated before `drafted → ready`. | Delivery Owner |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-007` | Dependencies are acyclic | Cycle detection in the edge write path of the dependency core. | Planning Platform Owner |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-008` | Constraints are declared, never implied | Validation core refuses to issue a verdict for a plan whose refusals cite undeclared constraints. | Constraint Authority |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-009` | Resource claims are claims, not allocations | Claim schema and the execution handoff contract, which exposes claims as requests only. | Capacity Authority |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-010` | Timelines are derived, never authored | Timeline core accepts derivation inputs only; no write path exists for timeline dates. | Planning Platform Owner |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-011` | No plan activates without a clear verdict | Activation guard in the lifecycle service, checking the verdict store for the exact version digest. | Lead Repository Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-012` | Activation requires dual authority | Lifecycle activation transition requiring two distinct roles from the agent registry. | Planning Owner Council |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-013` | Active plan versions are immutable | Repository write path rejects writes to versions in the active or monitored phase. | Planning Data Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-014` | Divergence tolerance is declared in advance | Activation guard requiring a tolerance object with critical-path and claim-overrun thresholds. | Plan Owner |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-015` | Replanning supersedes, never mutates | Replanning transition opens a new version through the repository version API. | Plan Owner |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-016` | Closure records an honest outcome | Closure transition requiring an outcome value and per-objective evaluations. | Planning Owner Council |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-017` | Every state change is a recorded transition | Write-path transition guard, which is the only path to a state change. | Planning Data Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-018` | Terminal states are terminal | Machine compiler rejects any outgoing edge from a declared terminal state. | Planning Data Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-019` | Records are append-only | Record store exposes append and read only. | Security Reviewer |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-020` | Every object carries complete metadata | Metadata validation in the write path, atomic with the body write. | Planning Data Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-021` | Traversal confers no access | Authorisation decision point at the repository contract layer, evaluated per landed object. | Security Reviewer |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-022` | Aggregates inherit the maximum classification | Aggregate authorisation constructs a synthetic object at the maximum input classification before deciding. | Security Reviewer |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-023` | Planning never executes | Architectural boundary review plus the absence of any dispatch capability in planning cores. | Lead Repository Architect |
| `CAT-PE-CONST-024` | Verdicts are reproducible | Validation core records the rule set version and input digest with every verdict. | Lead Repository Architect |

#### CAT-PE-CONST-001 — Intent precedes derivation

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-001`
- **Title:** Intent precedes derivation
- **Normative statement:** The planning engine MUST NOT derive a goal, objective, or task from an intent that has not been admitted with an accountable author and an explicit non-goal list.
- **Rationale:** Derivation without an admitted intent produces work whose purpose cannot be reconstructed, which makes every downstream prioritisation argument unresolvable.
- **Enforcement point:** Intent admission gate at the entry of the derivation core.
- **Violation behavior:** Derivation is refused, a refusal record is written naming the missing admission fields, and the caller receives `intent_not_admitted`.
- **Validation method:** Admission test suite asserting that derivation with a draft intent is refused.
- **Owner:** Planning Owner Council
- **Related concepts:** Intent layer, goal hierarchy, derivation receipts

#### CAT-PE-CONST-002 — Every derived object names its parent

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-002`
- **Title:** Every derived object names its parent
- **Normative statement:** Every goal, objective, task, and work package MUST carry a resolvable reference to the object one level above it.
- **Rationale:** An orphan object cannot be prioritised, cannot be closed on evidence, and silently consumes capacity that was committed to something else.
- **Enforcement point:** Reference resolution at the repository contract layer on every write.
- **Violation behavior:** The write is rejected with `orphan_object` naming the missing parent field; the object is never stored.
- **Validation method:** Orphan detection sweep over the ancestry index returning zero results.
- **Owner:** Planning Data Architect
- **Related concepts:** Goal hierarchy, objective hierarchy, task hierarchy, ancestry index

#### CAT-PE-CONST-003 — Goals are outcomes, not activities

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-003`
- **Title:** Goals are outcomes, not activities
- **Normative statement:** A goal MUST express a change in the world and MUST NOT be phrased as the execution of an activity, a project, or a deliverable.
- **Rationale:** Activity-shaped goals are satisfied by effort rather than by result, which converts the goal hierarchy into a task list with extra ceremony.
- **Enforcement point:** Goal admission review with a structural check for activity verbs and deliverable nouns.
- **Violation behavior:** Admission is refused with `goal_expressed_as_activity` and the proposing role is given the outcome question to answer.
- **Validation method:** Goal catalogue review asserting every live goal states an observable change.
- **Owner:** Goal Portfolio Owner
- **Related concepts:** Planning philosophy, goal hierarchy, objective hierarchy

#### CAT-PE-CONST-004 — Objectives are measurable or they are not objectives

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-004`
- **Title:** Objectives are measurable or they are not objectives
- **Normative statement:** Every objective MUST declare a metric, a baseline, a target, a measurement window, and a named evidence source before it becomes active.
- **Rationale:** Without a declared measurement contract, objective attainment becomes a matter of narrative, and closure becomes a negotiation rather than an observation.
- **Enforcement point:** Objective activation gate in the objective core.
- **Violation behavior:** Activation is refused with `unmeasurable_objective` listing the missing measurement fields.
- **Validation method:** Activation test suite asserting refusal for each individually missing field.
- **Owner:** Objective Steward
- **Related concepts:** Objective hierarchy, planning metadata, acceptance evidence

#### CAT-PE-CONST-005 — Baselines are frozen before measurement

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-005`
- **Title:** Baselines are frozen before measurement
- **Normative statement:** An objective baseline MUST be captured and frozen before the measurement window opens and MUST NOT be revised inside the window.
- **Rationale:** A movable baseline lets any result be presented as success and destroys the comparability that makes measurement worth doing.
- **Enforcement point:** Baseline freeze at objective activation, enforced by the immutability of the activated version.
- **Violation behavior:** The baseline edit is rejected; changing a baseline requires a superseding objective version with a recorded reason.
- **Validation method:** Version diff audit asserting no baseline field changed within an open window.
- **Owner:** Objective Steward
- **Related concepts:** Objective hierarchy, planning lifecycle, supersession

#### CAT-PE-CONST-006 — Tasks declare a definition of done

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-006`
- **Title:** Tasks declare a definition of done
- **Normative statement:** A task MUST NOT reach the ready state without a definition of done that names observable evidence.
- **Rationale:** Completion without declared evidence is completion by assertion, which is how blocked work is reported as finished and dependents start against nothing.
- **Enforcement point:** Readiness gate in the task core, evaluated before `drafted → ready`.
- **Violation behavior:** The readiness transition is refused with `no_definition_of_done` and the task remains drafted.
- **Validation method:** Readiness gate test suite covering each missing readiness field.
- **Owner:** Delivery Owner
- **Related concepts:** Task hierarchy, planning states, acceptance evidence

#### CAT-PE-CONST-007 — Dependencies are acyclic

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-007`
- **Title:** Dependencies are acyclic
- **Normative statement:** The dependency graph MUST remain acyclic; an edge that would create a cycle MUST be rejected at write time.
- **Rationale:** A cycle makes scheduling undefined and makes every downstream date a fiction, and cycles introduced silently are found only when the plan fails to converge.
- **Enforcement point:** Cycle detection in the edge write path of the dependency core.
- **Violation behavior:** The edge write is rejected with `cycle_detected` and the offending path is named in the refusal record.
- **Validation method:** Graph invariant check run on every write and as a periodic full-graph sweep.
- **Owner:** Planning Platform Owner
- **Related concepts:** Dependency layer, planning relationships, timeline derivation

#### CAT-PE-CONST-008 — Constraints are declared, never implied

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-008`
- **Title:** Constraints are declared, never implied
- **Normative statement:** Every constraint that bounds a plan MUST exist as a first-class constraint object with an issuing authority and an expiry or review date.
- **Rationale:** Undeclared constraints live in the heads of individuals, cannot be validated against, and reappear as surprise objections after commitments have been made.
- **Enforcement point:** Validation core refuses to issue a verdict for a plan whose refusals cite undeclared constraints.
- **Violation behavior:** The verdict is withheld with `undeclared_constraint` until the constraint is registered by an authorised role.
- **Validation method:** Constraint registry reconciliation against verdict refusal reasons.
- **Owner:** Constraint Authority
- **Related concepts:** Constraint layer, planning constitution, verdicts

#### CAT-PE-CONST-009 — Resource claims are claims, not allocations

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-009`
- **Title:** Resource claims are claims, not allocations
- **Normative statement:** A planning resource claim MUST represent an intent to consume capacity and MUST NOT be treated by any consumer as a guaranteed allocation.
- **Rationale:** Conflating claims with allocations makes the planning engine an execution scheduler, which is a boundary violation that produces two competing systems of record for capacity.
- **Enforcement point:** Claim schema and the execution handoff contract, which exposes claims as requests only.
- **Violation behavior:** A consumer treating a claim as an allocation is rejected at contract validation with `claim_treated_as_allocation`.
- **Validation method:** Contract conformance tests over the handoff surface.
- **Owner:** Capacity Authority
- **Related concepts:** Resource layer, execution handoff, planning philosophy

#### CAT-PE-CONST-010 — Timelines are derived, never authored

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-010`
- **Title:** Timelines are derived, never authored
- **Normative statement:** A plan timeline MUST be computed from tasks, dependencies, constraints, and claims, and MUST NOT be entered directly by any actor.
- **Rationale:** A hand-authored timeline encodes a wish rather than a consequence, and it hides the dependency or capacity problem that produced the impossible date.
- **Enforcement point:** Timeline core accepts derivation inputs only; no write path exists for timeline dates.
- **Violation behavior:** A direct timeline write is rejected with `timeline_not_derivable`; the caller is directed to change the inputs.
- **Validation method:** Timeline reproducibility test: recomputation from stored inputs yields an identical timeline digest.
- **Owner:** Planning Platform Owner
- **Related concepts:** Timeline layer, dependency layer, planning architecture

#### CAT-PE-CONST-011 — No plan activates without a clear verdict

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-011`
- **Title:** No plan activates without a clear verdict
- **Normative statement:** A plan version MUST NOT transition to active unless the validation core has published a passing constitutional verdict for that exact version.
- **Rationale:** Activating an unvalidated plan converts an unchecked document into an organisational commitment, which is the single most expensive failure mode in planning.
- **Enforcement point:** Activation guard in the lifecycle service, checking the verdict store for the exact version digest.
- **Violation behavior:** Activation is refused with `activation_without_clear_verdict`, and the refusal is recorded with both requested approvers.
- **Validation method:** Lifecycle test suite asserting refusal for failing, absent, and stale verdicts.
- **Owner:** Lead Repository Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning lifecycle, validation layer, verdict records

#### CAT-PE-CONST-012 — Activation requires dual authority

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-012`
- **Title:** Activation requires dual authority
- **Normative statement:** Activation MUST be approved jointly by the plan owner and the capacity authority, and both approvers MUST be recorded.
- **Rationale:** Activation commits both direction and capacity; a single approver can commit resources they do not hold, which surfaces as capacity conflict months later.
- **Enforcement point:** Lifecycle activation transition requiring two distinct roles from the agent registry.
- **Violation behavior:** Activation is refused with `insufficient_authority` naming the missing role.
- **Validation method:** Activation record audit asserting exactly two distinct approving roles on every activation.
- **Owner:** Planning Owner Council
- **Related concepts:** Planning lifecycle, resource layer, change records

#### CAT-PE-CONST-013 — Active plan versions are immutable

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-013`
- **Title:** Active plan versions are immutable
- **Normative statement:** An active plan version MUST NOT be edited; any change MUST produce a superseding version.
- **Rationale:** Editing an active plan erases the commitment that was actually made, which makes divergence undetectable and makes accountability retrospective fiction.
- **Enforcement point:** Repository write path rejects writes to versions in the active or monitored phase.
- **Violation behavior:** The write is rejected with `active_version_immutable` and replanning is proposed instead.
- **Validation method:** Store test suite asserting rejection for every field on an active version.
- **Owner:** Planning Data Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning repository, planning lifecycle, supersession

#### CAT-PE-CONST-014 — Divergence tolerance is declared in advance

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-014`
- **Title:** Divergence tolerance is declared in advance
- **Normative statement:** A plan MUST declare its divergence tolerance at activation, before any divergence exists.
- **Rationale:** A threshold agreed after the fact is a negotiation, not a control; declaring it in advance is what makes the replanning trigger objective.
- **Enforcement point:** Activation guard requiring a tolerance object with critical-path and claim-overrun thresholds.
- **Violation behavior:** Activation is refused with `activation_without_tolerance`.
- **Validation method:** Activation record audit asserting a tolerance object on every activation.
- **Owner:** Plan Owner
- **Related concepts:** Planning lifecycle, monitoring, replanning

#### CAT-PE-CONST-015 — Replanning supersedes, never mutates

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-015`
- **Title:** Replanning supersedes, never mutates
- **Normative statement:** Replanning MUST produce a new plan version that supersedes the prior one and MUST leave the prior version readable and unchanged.
- **Rationale:** Without supersession nobody can answer which plan was in force on a given date, which destroys both audit and learning.
- **Enforcement point:** Replanning transition opens a new version through the repository version API.
- **Violation behavior:** Any attempt to write replanning content onto the existing version is rejected with `replan_requires_supersession`.
- **Validation method:** Version chain audit asserting every replan produced a strictly increasing version with a recorded reason.
- **Owner:** Plan Owner
- **Related concepts:** Planning lifecycle, planning repository, change records

#### CAT-PE-CONST-016 — Closure records an honest outcome

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-016`
- **Title:** Closure records an honest outcome
- **Normative statement:** Plan closure MUST record an outcome from the defined set, including `not_met`, with matching evidence.
- **Rationale:** A system in which no plan ever closes as unmet has not achieved perfect planning; it has lost the ability to learn.
- **Enforcement point:** Closure transition requiring an outcome value and per-objective evaluations.
- **Violation behavior:** Closure is refused with `outcome_unsupported_by_evidence`.
- **Validation method:** Closure audit sampling outcomes against objective evaluation records.
- **Owner:** Planning Owner Council
- **Related concepts:** Planning lifecycle, objective hierarchy, planning records

#### CAT-PE-CONST-017 — Every state change is a recorded transition

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-017`
- **Title:** Every state change is a recorded transition
- **Normative statement:** Every planning object state change MUST be produced by a guarded transition and MUST write a record, including refusals.
- **Rationale:** Unrecorded state changes make the state machine advisory, and an advisory state machine is a status field with extra documentation.
- **Enforcement point:** Write-path transition guard, which is the only path to a state change.
- **Violation behavior:** Direct state assignment is rejected with `illegal_transition`; the attempt is recorded.
- **Validation method:** Record completeness check comparing state changes in the version stream to transition records.
- **Owner:** Planning Data Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning states, planning records, planning repository

#### CAT-PE-CONST-018 — Terminal states are terminal

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-018`
- **Title:** Terminal states are terminal
- **Normative statement:** A transition out of a terminal state MUST NOT exist in any compiled state machine.
- **Rationale:** Resurrectable completion makes completion counts, capacity releases, and rollups unreliable at all times, not just when a resurrection happens.
- **Enforcement point:** Machine compiler rejects any outgoing edge from a declared terminal state.
- **Violation behavior:** Compilation fails with `terminal_state_has_exit` and the machine is not loaded.
- **Validation method:** Compiler test suite covering terminal-state edges for every object type.
- **Owner:** Planning Data Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning states, planning objects, planning lifecycle

#### CAT-PE-CONST-019 — Records are append-only

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-019`
- **Title:** Records are append-only
- **Normative statement:** Planning records MUST NOT be modified or deleted before their retention class allows; corrections are new records that reference the original.
- **Rationale:** A mutable audit trail is not an audit trail, and the ability to correct history quietly is indistinguishable from the ability to falsify it.
- **Enforcement point:** Record store exposes append and read only.
- **Violation behavior:** Any update or delete attempt is rejected with `record_immutable` and raised to security review.
- **Validation method:** Record store contract review plus periodic digest chain verification.
- **Owner:** Security Reviewer
- **Related concepts:** Planning records, planning repository, planning metadata

#### CAT-PE-CONST-020 — Every object carries complete metadata

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-020`
- **Title:** Every object carries complete metadata
- **Normative statement:** Every planning object MUST carry descriptive, governance, provenance, and operational metadata, with no default classification.
- **Rationale:** Governance operates on metadata alone; a missing or defaulted classification is how restricted planning content reaches unintended audiences.
- **Enforcement point:** Metadata validation in the write path, atomic with the body write.
- **Violation behavior:** The write is rejected naming the missing group; any stored object without a classification is treated as restricted.
- **Validation method:** Metadata completeness sweep over the governance index returning zero gaps.
- **Owner:** Planning Data Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning metadata, planning repository, security model

#### CAT-PE-CONST-021 — Traversal confers no access

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-021`
- **Title:** Traversal confers no access
- **Normative statement:** Reaching a planning object through a relationship MUST NOT grant any access to it; every hop re-evaluates authorisation.
- **Rationale:** Reachability treated as permission is the most common authorisation hole in planning systems, because the graph connects commercially sensitive goals to widely shared tasks.
- **Enforcement point:** Authorisation decision point at the repository contract layer, evaluated per landed object.
- **Violation behavior:** The hop returns an unresolvable reference and a deny access record; no partial or redacted content is returned.
- **Validation method:** Traversal penetration tests from each low-privilege role toward restricted ancestors.
- **Owner:** Security Reviewer
- **Related concepts:** Planning relationships and security, planning metadata, access records

#### CAT-PE-CONST-022 — Aggregates inherit the maximum classification

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-022`
- **Title:** Aggregates inherit the maximum classification
- **Normative statement:** Any aggregate computed over planning objects MUST be classified at the maximum classification of its contributing inputs.
- **Rationale:** Totals and rollups reveal their parts; exempting aggregates from classification is a reliable way to publish restricted content in a summary.
- **Enforcement point:** Aggregate authorisation constructs a synthetic object at the maximum input classification before deciding.
- **Violation behavior:** The aggregate request is denied at the restricted classification with `aggregate_classification_exceeds_grant`.
- **Validation method:** Aggregate authorisation tests mixing classifications across every rollup surface.
- **Owner:** Security Reviewer
- **Related concepts:** Planning relationships and security, planning metadata, goal rollups

#### CAT-PE-CONST-023 — Planning never executes

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-023`
- **Title:** Planning never executes
- **Normative statement:** The planning engine MUST NOT dispatch, schedule, or perform work; it MUST publish an execution handoff contract and stop at that boundary.
- **Rationale:** A planning engine that executes becomes the orchestrator, and the organisation loses the independent record of what was intended as distinct from what happened.
- **Enforcement point:** Architectural boundary review plus the absence of any dispatch capability in planning cores.
- **Violation behavior:** The offending call path is removed and the handoff contract is corrected; a boundary violation record is written.
- **Validation method:** Dependency and capability audit asserting no planning core imports an execution client.
- **Owner:** Lead Repository Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning philosophy, planning architecture, execution handoff

#### CAT-PE-CONST-024 — Verdicts are reproducible

- **Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-024`
- **Title:** Verdicts are reproducible
- **Normative statement:** A constitutional verdict MUST be reproducible from the stored plan version and the recorded rule set version alone.
- **Rationale:** A verdict that cannot be recomputed is an opinion with a timestamp, and it cannot support either audit or appeal.
- **Enforcement point:** Validation core records the rule set version and input digest with every verdict.
- **Violation behavior:** A non-reproducible verdict is voided, the plan returns to validated-pending, and the rule set discrepancy is investigated.
- **Validation method:** Scheduled recomputation of a sample of verdicts, comparing digests.
- **Owner:** Lead Repository Architect
- **Related concepts:** Planning constitution, planning records, planning repository

### Operational Stories

Four story types are recorded for `Planning Constitution`: a normal-path story, a failure story, a recovery story, and an audit story. Together they describe what this section looks like in operation.

**Normal path.** A planning owner performs the primary action this section governs, every guard passes, a receipt is written, and the resulting object is visible to the roles that hold grants for it within the published projection lag.

**Failure.** A guard refuses the action because a required field, reference, authority, or piece of evidence is absent. The refusal is recorded with its reason code, the caller is told exactly what is missing, and nothing partial is stored.

**Recovery.** The missing element is supplied and the action is retried, or, where the object is already stored, a superseding version is written with a recorded reason. No operator edits stored state directly, and no refusal is deleted.

**Audit.** An auditor reconstructs the sequence from the records this section writes, confirming who acted, under which rule set version, with which evidence, and what the outcome was — without asking anyone what happened.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Constitution`, the owning implementation MUST make this operational story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operating Contract

The operating contract for `Planning Constitution` is the short form of everything above, and it is what an on-call engineer reads at three in the morning.

| Clause | Commitment |
|---|---|
| Guarantee | Every accepted write satisfies the controls in this section and produces a receipt. |
| Refusal | Every refusal names a reason code and is recorded; nothing partial is stored. |
| Owner | Lead Repository Architect and Documentation Owner |
| Evidence | `planning constitutional receipt` |
| Escalation | Section owner, then the Planning Owner Council, then the Lead Repository Architect. |
| Degradation | Fail closed: refuse and record rather than proceed on an assumption. |

**Normative application:** For `Planning Constitution`, the owning implementation MUST make this contractual commitment observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

The procedure below is the full constitutional path for `Planning Constitution`, from request to evidence. It is the sequence auditors replay.

1. The requesting role submits the action with its inputs and its claimed authority.
2. The contract layer validates structure, references, tenancy, and metadata completeness.
3. The section's guards evaluate in order, each producing a pass or a named refusal reason.
4. On refusal the reason is recorded, the caller is informed, and processing stops with nothing stored.
5. On pass the new version is appended, never updated in place, with a monotonic version number.
6. The receipt named by this section is written and linked to the version digest.
7. A fact is published to the event boundary for consumers that do not need to block.
8. Projections rebuild and publish their lag, making the change visible to grant-holding roles.
9. The action becomes replayable: any auditor can recompute the outcome from stored inputs alone.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Constitution`, the owning implementation MUST make this procedural step observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Required Decision Record

Any change to `Planning Constitution` requires a decision record containing the following fields. A change proposed without them is returned unreviewed.

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Decision ID | A new ADR identifier in `adr/` |
| Superseded clause | The exact control or requirement ID being changed |
| Rationale | Why the current behaviour is insufficient, with evidence |
| Impact | Which cores, records, and grants change as a result |
| Migration | How existing objects pinned to the current version are handled |
| Approver | The section owner plus the Lead Repository Architect |
| Validation | How the new behaviour will be tested before it takes effect |

**Normative application:** For `Planning Constitution`, the owning implementation MUST make this decision requirement observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Normative Requirements

Each requirement below is binding for `Planning Constitution` and is paired with the evidence that demonstrates compliance.

| Requirement ID | Title | Normative statement | Compliance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CAT-PE-P1-03-R01` | Complete catalogue | The Part 1 constitution MUST enumerate every foundational rule with all nine required fields. | Document validation asserts nine fields per rule identifier. |

| `CAT-PE-P1-03-R06` | Named supersession | A rule MUST only be superseded by an accepted ADR that names its identifier. | Supersession without a named identifier fails review. |

**Normative application:** For `Planning Constitution`, the owning implementation MUST make this requirement observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Constitutional Control Catalogue

#### CAT-PE-P1-03-C01 — Complete catalogue

- **Rule:** The Part 1 constitution MUST enumerate every foundational rule with all nine required fields.
- **Business test:** A reviewer can confirm this holds by inspecting one real object without asking anyone.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Document validation asserts nine fields per rule identifier.
- **AI behavior:** The agent verifies this condition before proposing a write and reports it in the change description.
- **Human boundary:** A human MAY waive this only with a recorded, expiring waiver from Lead Repository Architect and Documentation Owner.
- **Security assertion:** Violation of this control widens exposure or removes an audit guarantee, so it fails closed.
- **Performance assertion:** The check is local to the object and its direct references and stays inside the write budget.

### Future Evolution

`Planning Constitution` evolves in three predictable directions. Second, the proposed repository paths become real cores with independent deployment lifecycles, at which point the contracts in this section become the only coupling between them. Third, the evidence this section produces becomes an input to automated portfolio analysis, which requires no change to the records themselves because they were designed to be read by machines that did not write them.

## 4. Planning Principles

**Section ID:** `CAT-PE-P1-04`  
**Constitutional domain:** Planning Principle Governance  
**Human accountable owner:** Lead Repository Architect and Documentation Owner  
**Primary record:** planning principle receipt  
**Decision status:** Foundation decision; evidence-gated. Later ADRs MUST preserve the behaviour specified here unless they explicitly supersede a named clause.  
**Primary question:** When two correct-looking planning designs conflict, which principle decides — and how is that decision recorded?

### Purpose

Principles are the tie-breakers of planning design. Where the constitution says what may never happen, principles say which of two permitted designs is preferred and why. This section states the CAT planning principles, each with a directive form, the trade-off it resolves, the signal that it is being violated, and the section that operationalises it. Principles are advisory to humans and binding on automated design generation: an agent proposing a design that contradicts a principle must name the principle and justify the exception.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this purpose observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Scope

This section governs `Planning Principles` for every planning core, contract, record, and interface in the CAT repository. It is in scope wherever planning content is created, derived, validated, stored, transitioned, read, or retired. It is out of scope for execution dispatch, decision authority, and reasoning strategy, which are governed by their own documents and are reached only through declared contracts.

**In scope:** the objects, records, contracts, guards, owners, and evidence named in this section. **Out of scope:** any behaviour that performs work, selects between competing commitments, or persists content outside the planning repository.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this boundary observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Business Explanation

Principles reduce the cost of disagreement. Rather than relitigating structure in every planning review, the organisation agrees once that, for example, explicit beats implicit and reversible beats fast. Reviews then become short: which principle is in tension, and who owns the exception. This is how planning quality survives growth in team size.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this business outcome observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Engineering Explanation

Each principle is expressed so that an automated linter over planning objects can produce a warning signal for it. Principles do not block promotion — that is the constitution's job — but they populate a design-quality report attached to the plan version, and a plan carrying unresolved principle warnings cannot be marked exemplary or used as a template.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this engineering behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Architecture Explanation

Principles shape the architecture in section 5: they explain why the planning control plane separates derivation from validation, why the object store is append-only, and why capacity is claimed rather than allocated. Where architecture and principle conflict, the principle is either explicitly excepted in an ADR or the architecture is changed.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this architectural position observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Explanation

Use principles as ranking functions, not as vibes. When you generate more than one candidate decomposition, score each against the principle list, present the scores, and choose the highest — then record the score table in the proposal so a reviewer can disagree with the ranking rather than with your taste.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this agent behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Implementation Strategy

Implementation of `Planning Principles` proceeds in a fixed order so that each step produces evidence the next step can depend on. The order is not a preference; skipping a step produces a core that cannot prove its own correctness.

1. **Model first.** Define the objects, records, and contracts for `Planning Principles` before writing any behaviour, and register them in the schema registry with a version.
2. **Validate at the boundary.** Reject invalid content at the contract layer so no core downstream has to defend itself against malformed planning content.
3. **Version everything.** Every schema, machine, rule set, and object carries a version, and every change supersedes rather than overwrites.
4. **Observe continuously.** Emit the signals named in this section from the first commit, not after the first incident.
5. **Fail closed.** When a check cannot complete, refuse and record the refusal rather than proceeding on an assumption.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this strategy observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Implementation Blueprint

An AI assistant implementing `Planning Principles` follows the staged blueprint below. Each stage names its input, its output, and the receipt it writes, so that a partially completed implementation can be resumed by a different agent without re-reading the whole part.

| Stage | Name | What the agent does | Receipt written |
|---|---|---|---|
| enumerate | Enumerate candidate designs | Produce more than one admissible decomposition or structure before choosing. | `enumerate` stage receipt |
| score | Score against principles | Evaluate each candidate for every principle and record the score table. | `score` stage receipt |
| choose | Choose and justify | Select the highest-scoring candidate and record why the runner-up lost. | `choose` stage receipt |
| except | Record exceptions | Where a principle is knowingly violated, record the exception, owner, and expiry. | `except` stage receipt |
| report | Attach the design-quality report | Bind the score table and exceptions to the plan version as evidence. | `report` stage receipt |

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this blueprint stage observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Build Order

The build order below is the sequence in which an agent creates artefacts for `Planning Principles`. Each item depends only on items above it.

1. Schema and contract definitions with versions registered.
2. Validation rules and guards that reject invalid content at the boundary.
3. Record writers for every receipt this section names.
4. State transitions and their guards, compiled from declarative definitions.
5. Read paths and projections, rebuildable from the version stream.
6. Observability signals for every failure mode listed in this section.
7. Acceptance tests drawn from this section's test list, run in continuous integration.

### Monitoring and Observability

Observability for `Planning Principles` is defined by the failure modes below: every failure mode has a detection signal, and every detection signal is emitted by the implementation rather than inferred by an operator. A failure mode with no signal is an unmonitored failure mode and is treated as a gap.

- **Counters:** accepted writes, rejected writes by reason code, refused transitions by reason code.
- **Gauges:** open objects by state, objects awaiting evidence, grant and waiver expiry horizon.
- **Histograms:** guard evaluation duration, derivation duration, record write duration.
- **Traces:** one span per stage in the blueprint above, correlated by plan identity.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this signal observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Runtime Behaviour

At runtime, `Planning Principles` behaves as a synchronous guard on the write path and an asynchronous emitter on the event path. Writes are validated, recorded, and either accepted or refused within the write budget; facts about accepted writes are published afterwards for consumers that do not need to block. Nothing in this section performs work, calls an execution surface, or blocks on a remote decision.

### Risks

| Risk | Impact if unmanaged | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Principles multiply until they conflict routinely | Ranking becomes arbitrary | Keep the catalogue small and state each trade-off explicitly |
| Authors game the scores | Design quality reports lose meaning | Reviewers challenge the score table, not just the outcome |
| Exceptions never expire | Principles quietly stop applying | Every exception carries an expiry and a re-justification requirement |
| Principles are cited to block work | Reviews stall on preference | Only constitutional rules may block promotion |
| Automated design ignores principles | Machine-generated plans regress in quality | Agents must attach a score table to every generated design |

### Anti-patterns

- **Principles written as slogans.** 'Be pragmatic' cannot rank two designs.
- **Scoring after the decision.** A score table produced to justify a chosen design is theatre.
- **Hidden trade-offs.** A principle that never loses to another is not a principle, it is a rule.
- **Exception by omission.** Silently violating a principle deprives reviewers of the trade-off.
- **Using principles to block promotion.** Confusing advice with law makes both weaker.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this prohibition observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Best Practices

- Always generate at least two admissible candidates before choosing.
- State which principle lost, not only which one won.
- Attach the score table to the plan version, not to a chat message.
- Expire exceptions and force re-justification.
- Keep the principle catalogue short enough that a reviewer holds it in memory.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this practice observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Examples

An agent proposes two decompositions for a payout-reconciliation objective: one with three coarse tasks and one with nine fine-grained tasks. It scores both, notes that fine-grained wins on observability and loses on coordination overhead, chooses the fine-grained option, records the trade-off, and attaches the table. The reviewer disagrees on one score, the table is amended, and the decision is re-derived in minutes rather than debated for an hour.

The following example is illustrative and shortened; it is not production data.

```json

  "candidates": [
```

### Counter Examples

The same agent emits one decomposition with the note 'this seems reasonable'. The reviewer has nothing to argue with except the output itself, so review becomes taste. Six weeks later nobody can reconstruct why the plan was shaped that way, and the next agent regenerates a different shape for the same objective.

```json
  "object": "rejected_planning_principles_example",
```

- **Rejected:** The chosen candidate is required to record why the runner-up lost.

### Pseudo Code

The logic below is complete for the behaviour it describes; it contains no omission markers and can be transliterated into any of the languages named in Section 5.

```text
function choose_design(candidates, principle_set):
    if len(candidates) < 2:
        return reject("single_candidate_design", "a choice requires alternatives")

    table = ScoreTable(principle_set_version = principle_set.version)

    for candidate in candidates:
        row = {}
        total = 0
        for principle in principle_set.principles:
            score = principle.evaluate(candidate)      # 0..3, deterministic
            row[principle.id] = score
            total = total + score * principle.weight
        table.add(candidate.id, row, total)

    ranked = table.sort_descending_by_total()
    winner = ranked[0]
    runner_up = ranked[1]

    losing_principles = []
    for principle in principle_set.principles:
        if table.score(runner_up.id, principle.id) > table.score(winner.id, principle.id):
            losing_principles.append(principle.id)

    table.chosen = winner.id
    table.runner_up_rationale = describe_tradeoff(runner_up.id, losing_principles)

    for principle in principle_set.principles:
        if table.score(winner.id, principle.id) == 0:
            exception = exception_store.find(winner.id, principle.id)
            if exception is None or exception.expired():
                table.warnings.append(principle.id)

    attach_to_plan_version(winner.plan_version, table)
    return winner
```

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this algorithm observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Planning Principle Catalogue

The principles below are the complete principle set for CAT planning. A principle is not a rule: it does not have an enforcement point of its own, and it is not cited in refusal messages. It is the reasoning that produced the rules, and it is what an engineer or agent applies when a situation arises that no rule anticipated. Each principle names the tension it lives with, because a principle with no cost is usually a slogan.

| Principle ID | Name | One-line statement |
|---|---|---|
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-001` | Purpose before plan | No planning structure is created before the intent it serves is admitted and written down. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-002` | Outcomes over activities | Planning expresses intended changes in the world, and derives activity from them rather than the reverse. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-003` | Evidence over assertion | Every claim of readiness, progress, or completion is backed by named, fetchable evidence. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-004` | Derivation over declaration | Anything computable from other planning content is computed, not typed in. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-005` | Supersede, never overwrite | Change produces a new version; the previous version remains readable forever. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-006` | Fail closed | When a check cannot be completed, planning refuses rather than proceeding optimistically. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-007` | Ownership is a role, never a person | Every planning object is owned by a role defined in the agent registry. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-008` | Boundaries are explicit | Planning states what it does not do, and hands off at a declared contract. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-009` | Measure the window, not the moment | Objective attainment is judged over a declared window with a frozen baseline. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-010` | Small enough to finish | Tasks are decomposed until each can be completed by one owner within one cadence. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-011` | Coverage and exclusivity together | A work breakdown must cover all in-scope work exactly once, with no gaps and no overlaps. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-012` | Classification is a decision, not a default | Every planning object is deliberately classified at write time. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-013` | Reachability is not permission | Access is granted explicitly per role and per operation, never inherited through relationships. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-014` | Records outlive systems | Planning records are written so that they remain interpretable without the software that produced them. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-015` | One system of record | The planning repository is the only authoritative source; every other view is derived and rebuildable. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-016` | Declare tolerance before divergence | The threshold at which a plan stops describing reality is set at activation. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-017` | Honest closure | Plans close with the outcome that occurred, including unmet. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-018` | Multi-core, multi-language by construction | Planning capability is delivered as bounded cores communicating through contracts, in whichever language suits each core. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-019` | Deterministic where it matters | Derivation, validation, and scheduling produce identical outputs for identical inputs. |
| `CAT-PE-PRIN-020` | Plans are read more than written | Planning content is optimised for comprehension by humans and machines that did not write it. |

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-001 — Purpose before plan

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-001`
- **Statement:** No planning structure is created before the intent it serves is admitted and written down.
- **Rationale:** Structure created ahead of purpose acquires its own momentum and becomes very hard to retire.
- **Applies to:** Intent admission, goal derivation
- **Tension:** Speed: teams want to start structuring during the conversation that produces intent.
- **Resolution:** Admission is cheap and takes minutes; it is a gate, not a phase.
- **Observable test:** Every live goal resolves to an admitted intent with a non-goal list.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-002 — Outcomes over activities

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-002`
- **Statement:** Planning expresses intended changes in the world, and derives activity from them rather than the reverse.
- **Rationale:** Activity-first planning produces busy organisations that cannot say what changed.
- **Applies to:** Goal hierarchy, objective hierarchy
- **Tension:** Activities are concrete and easy to agree on; outcomes invite argument.
- **Resolution:** The argument is the value; having it at goal definition is far cheaper than having it at closure.
- **Observable test:** No live goal is phrased as a deliverable or a project name.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-003 — Evidence over assertion

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-003`
- **Statement:** Every claim of readiness, progress, or completion is backed by named, fetchable evidence.
- **Rationale:** Assertion-based status is the mechanism by which organisations discover problems late.
- **Applies to:** Objective measurement, task completion, verdicts
- **Tension:** Evidence collection has a cost, and some outcomes are genuinely hard to measure.
- **Resolution:** Hard-to-measure outcomes declare proxy metrics explicitly rather than skipping measurement.
- **Observable test:** Every completed task and met objective names its evidence source.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-004 — Derivation over declaration

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-004`
- **Statement:** Anything computable from other planning content is computed, not typed in.
- **Rationale:** Typed-in derived values drift from their inputs and hide the real constraint.
- **Applies to:** Timelines, rollups, critical paths, capacity totals
- **Tension:** Derived values sometimes produce answers people do not want.
- **Resolution:** Change the inputs, not the output; the unwanted answer is information.
- **Observable test:** Timeline and rollup digests recompute identically from stored inputs.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-005 — Supersede, never overwrite

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-005`
- **Statement:** Change produces a new version; the previous version remains readable forever.
- **Rationale:** Overwriting destroys the ability to say what was committed and when it changed.
- **Applies to:** All planning objects and records
- **Tension:** Version chains grow storage and can complicate simple reads.
- **Resolution:** Head reads are cheap; retention classes bound the growth.
- **Observable test:** No in-place update path exists in the repository contract.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-006 — Fail closed

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-006`
- **Statement:** When a check cannot be completed, planning refuses rather than proceeding optimistically.
- **Rationale:** A planning system that degrades to permissive behaviour under stress fails exactly when its guarantees matter most.
- **Applies to:** Validation, authorisation, transition guards
- **Tension:** Refusal blocks work and creates pressure to add bypasses.
- **Resolution:** Bypasses are replaced by explicit, recorded, expiring waivers from a named authority.
- **Observable test:** Every unavailable dependency path is tested to deny or refuse, never to permit.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-007 — Ownership is a role, never a person

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-007`
- **Statement:** Every planning object is owned by a role defined in the agent registry.
- **Rationale:** People change teams; commitments outlive them, and person-keyed ownership silently orphans work.
- **Applies to:** All planning objects, grants, escalation paths
- **Tension:** Roles feel bureaucratic for small teams.
- **Resolution:** A role may currently have exactly one holder; the indirection still preserves continuity.
- **Observable test:** No owner or grant field resolves to an individual identity.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-008 — Boundaries are explicit

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-008`
- **Statement:** Planning states what it does not do, and hands off at a declared contract.
- **Rationale:** Undeclared boundaries get colonised, and the planning engine slowly becomes the orchestrator.
- **Applies to:** Execution handoff, decision engine interface, scheduling
- **Tension:** It is often faster in the moment to absorb the neighbouring responsibility.
- **Resolution:** Absorbed responsibilities become permanent; the handoff contract is the cheaper long-run choice.
- **Observable test:** No planning core holds a capability to dispatch or perform work.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-009 — Measure the window, not the moment

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-009`
- **Statement:** Objective attainment is judged over a declared window with a frozen baseline.
- **Rationale:** Point-in-time readings reward timing and noise rather than change.
- **Applies to:** Objective hierarchy, monitoring
- **Tension:** Windows delay the moment of judgement.
- **Resolution:** Interim readings are published continuously; only the verdict waits for the window.
- **Observable test:** Every objective declares baseline, target, and window before activation.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-010 — Small enough to finish

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-010`
- **Statement:** Tasks are decomposed until each can be completed by one owner within one cadence.
- **Rationale:** Oversized tasks hide their own risk and report progress that cannot be verified.
- **Applies to:** Task hierarchy, work breakdown structure
- **Tension:** Decomposition has overhead and can fragment coherent work.
- **Resolution:** Work packages preserve coherence while tasks stay finishable.
- **Observable test:** No ready task exceeds the declared cadence bound without a recorded exception.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-011 — Coverage and exclusivity together

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-011`
- **Statement:** A work breakdown must cover all in-scope work exactly once, with no gaps and no overlaps.
- **Rationale:** Gaps become unowned surprises; overlaps become duplicated effort and conflicting ownership.
- **Applies to:** Work breakdown structure
- **Tension:** Perfect exclusivity is hard when work genuinely shares surface area.
- **Resolution:** Shared surface is named as an explicit interface task with a single owner.
- **Observable test:** Coverage and overlap reports both pass before validation.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-012 — Classification is a decision, not a default

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-012`
- **Statement:** Every planning object is deliberately classified at write time.
- **Rationale:** Defaults become the classification of everything, including what should have been restricted.
- **Applies to:** Planning metadata, security model
- **Tension:** Deliberate classification slows down every write slightly.
- **Resolution:** The vocabulary is short and the decision is usually obvious; ambiguity resolves to restricted.
- **Observable test:** No write succeeds without an explicit classification.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-013 — Reachability is not permission

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-013`
- **Statement:** Access is granted explicitly per role and per operation, never inherited through relationships.
- **Rationale:** The planning graph deliberately connects sensitive intent to widely shared work.
- **Applies to:** Planning relationships and security
- **Tension:** Explicit grants require maintenance as structures evolve.
- **Resolution:** Grants are role-scoped and expiring, so maintenance is a scheduled review rather than an emergency.
- **Observable test:** Low-privilege roles cannot reach restricted ancestors through any traversal.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-014 — Records outlive systems

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-014`
- **Statement:** Planning records are written so that they remain interpretable without the software that produced them.
- **Rationale:** Audits and disputes routinely outlast the tools involved.
- **Applies to:** Planning records, planning metadata
- **Tension:** Self-describing records are more verbose than compact internal formats.
- **Resolution:** Verbosity is cheap relative to the cost of an uninterpretable audit trail.
- **Observable test:** A record sample is interpretable using only the record and this document.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-015 — One system of record

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-015`
- **Statement:** The planning repository is the only authoritative source; every other view is derived and rebuildable.
- **Rationale:** Competing sources of truth turn every discrepancy into an investigation.
- **Applies to:** Planning repository, read models, exports
- **Tension:** Teams want to maintain their own spreadsheets and boards.
- **Resolution:** Derived views are supported and rebuildable, so local views stay consistent by construction.
- **Observable test:** Every read model rebuilds from the version stream to an identical digest.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-016 — Declare tolerance before divergence

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-016`
- **Statement:** The threshold at which a plan stops describing reality is set at activation.
- **Rationale:** Thresholds negotiated after divergence appears are set by discomfort rather than by judgement.
- **Applies to:** Planning lifecycle, monitoring
- **Tension:** Setting a number in advance feels arbitrary.
- **Resolution:** An arbitrary declared number is more useful than an unstated one, and it can be superseded deliberately.
- **Observable test:** Every activation record carries a tolerance object.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-017 — Honest closure

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-017`
- **Statement:** Plans close with the outcome that occurred, including unmet.
- **Rationale:** Systems that cannot record failure cannot produce learning.
- **Applies to:** Planning lifecycle, objective evaluation
- **Tension:** Recording unmet outcomes has social cost.
- **Resolution:** The outcome attaches to the plan and its evidence, not to an individual.
- **Observable test:** Closure outcomes are distributed across the defined set, not uniformly met.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-018 — Multi-core, multi-language by construction

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-018`
- **Statement:** Planning capability is delivered as bounded cores communicating through contracts, in whichever language suits each core.
- **Rationale:** A single-language monolith constrains hiring, performance, and independent evolution.
- **Applies to:** Planning architecture
- **Tension:** Polyglot systems cost more in tooling and shared libraries.
- **Resolution:** Contracts are language-neutral and generated, so the cost is bounded and one-time per core.
- **Observable test:** No planning contract depends on a single runtime's serialisation format.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-019 — Deterministic where it matters

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-019`
- **Statement:** Derivation, validation, and scheduling produce identical outputs for identical inputs.
- **Rationale:** Non-determinism in planning makes verdicts unappealable and defects unreproducible.
- **Applies to:** Derivation core, validation core, timeline core
- **Tension:** Model-assisted drafting is inherently non-deterministic.
- **Resolution:** Models draft candidates; deterministic cores decide, and the decision is what is recorded.
- **Observable test:** Recomputation of sampled verdicts and timelines yields identical digests.

#### CAT-PE-PRIN-020 — Plans are read more than written

- **Principle ID:** `CAT-PE-PRIN-020`
- **Statement:** Planning content is optimised for comprehension by humans and machines that did not write it.
- **Rationale:** Most of a plan's life is spent being read by people who were not in the room.
- **Applies to:** All planning objects and this document
- **Tension:** Comprehensible content is longer to author.
- **Resolution:** Authoring cost is paid once; reading cost is paid continuously by many.
- **Observable test:** A reader unfamiliar with the plan can state its intent, owner, and evidence within one page.

### Operational Stories

Four story types are recorded for `Planning Principles`: a normal-path story, a failure story, a recovery story, and an audit story. Together they describe what this section looks like in operation.

**Normal path.** A planning owner performs the primary action this section governs, every guard passes, a receipt is written, and the resulting object is visible to the roles that hold grants for it within the published projection lag.

**Failure.** A guard refuses the action because a required field, reference, authority, or piece of evidence is absent. The refusal is recorded with its reason code, the caller is told exactly what is missing, and nothing partial is stored.

**Recovery.** The missing element is supplied and the action is retried, or, where the object is already stored, a superseding version is written with a recorded reason. No operator edits stored state directly, and no refusal is deleted.

**Audit.** An auditor reconstructs the sequence from the records this section writes, confirming who acted, under which rule set version, with which evidence, and what the outcome was — without asking anyone what happened.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this operational story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operating Contract

The operating contract for `Planning Principles` is the short form of everything above, and it is what an on-call engineer reads at three in the morning.

| Clause | Commitment |
|---|---|
| Guarantee | Every accepted write satisfies the controls in this section and produces a receipt. |
| Refusal | Every refusal names a reason code and is recorded; nothing partial is stored. |
| Owner | Lead Repository Architect and Documentation Owner |
| Evidence | `planning principle receipt` |
| Escalation | Section owner, then the Planning Owner Council, then the Lead Repository Architect. |
| Degradation | Fail closed: refuse and record rather than proceed on an assumption. |

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this contractual commitment observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

The procedure below is the full constitutional path for `Planning Principles`, from request to evidence. It is the sequence auditors replay.

1. The requesting role submits the action with its inputs and its claimed authority.
2. The contract layer validates structure, references, tenancy, and metadata completeness.
3. The section's guards evaluate in order, each producing a pass or a named refusal reason.
4. On refusal the reason is recorded, the caller is informed, and processing stops with nothing stored.
5. On pass the new version is appended, never updated in place, with a monotonic version number.
6. The receipt named by this section is written and linked to the version digest.
7. A fact is published to the event boundary for consumers that do not need to block.
8. Projections rebuild and publish their lag, making the change visible to grant-holding roles.
9. The action becomes replayable: any auditor can recompute the outcome from stored inputs alone.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this procedural step observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Required Decision Record

Any change to `Planning Principles` requires a decision record containing the following fields. A change proposed without them is returned unreviewed.

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Decision ID | A new ADR identifier in `adr/` |
| Superseded clause | The exact control or requirement ID being changed |
| Rationale | Why the current behaviour is insufficient, with evidence |
| Impact | Which cores, records, and grants change as a result |
| Migration | How existing objects pinned to the current version are handled |
| Approver | The section owner plus the Lead Repository Architect |
| Validation | How the new behaviour will be tested before it takes effect |

**Normative application:** For `Planning Principles`, the owning implementation MUST make this decision requirement observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

#### CAT-PE-P1-04-C01 — Multiple candidates

- **Rule:** A generated planning design MUST present at least two admissible candidates with scores.
- **Business test:** A reviewer can confirm this holds by inspecting one real object without asking anyone.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Design intake rejects score tables with fewer than two candidates.
- **AI behavior:** The agent verifies this condition before proposing a write and reports it in the change description.
- **Human boundary:** A human MAY waive this only with a recorded, expiring waiver from Lead Repository Architect and Documentation Owner.
- **Security assertion:** Violation of this control widens exposure or removes an audit guarantee, so it fails closed.
- **Performance assertion:** The check is local to the object and its direct references and stays inside the write budget.
- **Evidence:** `planning principle receipt`
- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P1_04_C01`
- **Recovery:** Supply the missing element and retry, or supersede the stored version with a recorded reason.
- **Implementation test:** Automated test asserting both the accepted and the refused path for this rule.

### Diagrams

Each diagram below is preceded by its identifier, title, purpose, audience, and reading order. Diagrams are normative where they show ordering or authority; they are illustrative where they show grouping.

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P1-S04-D001`  
**Title:** Principle ranking flow  
**Purpose:** Show how candidates are scored, chosen, and excepted.  
**Audience:** Plan authors, reviewers  
**Reading order:** Follow top to bottom; the exception branch is the only path that tolerates a zero score.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C[Candidate designs >= 2] --> S[Score every principle for every candidate]
    S --> R[Rank by weighted total]
    R --> W[Winner selected]
    W --> Q{Any principle scored zero?}
    Q -- no --> EX[Exemplary - usable as template]
    Q -- yes --> E{Approved exception exists?}
    E -- yes --> OK[Accepted with recorded exception and expiry]
    E -- no --> WARN[Design-quality warning attached to plan version]
    WARN --> RE[Return to author for re-design or exception request]
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P1-S04-D002`  
**Title:** Principle versus rule authority  
**Purpose:** Clarify that principles rank and rules block.  
**Audience:** All readers  
**Reading order:** Left path is advisory, right path is binding.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P[Principle evaluation] --> PW[Warning on design-quality report]
    PW --> PA[Promotion still permitted]
    R[Constitutional rule evaluation] --> RV[Violation]
    RV --> RB[Promotion blocked and plan quarantined]
    PA --> H[Handoff]
    RB --> Q[Owner remediation]
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P1-S04-D003`  
**Title:** Exception lifecycle  
**Purpose:** Show how a principle exception is granted, expires, and forces re-justification.  
**Audience:** Planning owners  
**Reading order:** Note that expiry returns the plan to a warning state rather than to compliance.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> compliant
    compliant --> warned: principle scored zero
    warned --> excepted: owner approves with expiry
    excepted --> warned: exception expires
    warned --> compliant: design changed to satisfy principle
    excepted --> compliant: design changed before expiry
    compliant --> [*]
```

## 5. Planning Architecture

**Section ID:** `CAT-PE-P1-05`  
**Constitutional domain:** Planning Platform Architecture  
**Human accountable owner:** Head of Planning Platform and Lead Repository Architect  
**Primary record:** planning architecture receipt  
**Decision status:** Foundation decision; evidence-gated. Later ADRs MUST preserve the behaviour specified here unless they explicitly supersede a named clause.  
**Primary question:** What are the components of the planning platform, in which languages and processes do they live, and how does the same design run as one process today and as a Kubernetes deployment later?

### Purpose

This section defines the component architecture of the CAT planning platform: the cores, their responsibilities, the contracts between them, the language boundaries, and the deployment evolution from a single process to a multi-service, Kubernetes-ready topology. The architecture is deliberately multi-core and multi-language: derivation, validation, persistence, and handoff have different performance, safety, and iteration characteristics, and CAT does not pretend one runtime suits all four.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this purpose observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Scope

This section governs `Planning Architecture` for every planning core, contract, record, and interface in the CAT repository. It is in scope wherever planning content is created, derived, validated, stored, transitioned, read, or retired. It is out of scope for execution dispatch, decision authority, and reasoning strategy, which are governed by their own documents and are reached only through declared contracts.

**In scope:** the objects, records, contracts, guards, owners, and evidence named in this section. **Out of scope:** any behaviour that performs work, selects between competing commitments, or persists content outside the planning repository.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this boundary observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Business Explanation

A multi-core architecture is what allows planning to start cheap and scale without a rewrite. The business can run the whole platform in one process during early delivery and later move only the parts under pressure — usually validation and timeline derivation — onto their own footprint, without renegotiating contracts or retraining teams on new semantics.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this business outcome observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Engineering Explanation

Six cores are defined: the Intake Core (admission and normalisation), the Derivation Core (goal, objective, task, and dependency derivation), the Constraint Core (constraint binding and capacity claims), the Timeline Core (schedule derivation), the Validation Core (structural, semantic, constitutional validation), and the Handoff Core (execution contract publication). Cores communicate through versioned typed contracts and are individually deployable. Language selection is by workload: Python for derivation and analytical logic where the ecosystem is strongest, TypeScript for API, SDK, and collaboration surfaces, Go or Rust for the deterministic, latency-sensitive validation and timeline cores when they are extracted, and SQL for the plan store's invariants.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this engineering behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Architecture Explanation

The cores form a directed pipeline with a shared append-only object store and an event boundary onto `context/08_EVENTS_SYSTEM.md`. No core writes another core's objects; each owns its outputs and publishes them. The control plane is separated from the data plane so that a slow derivation never blocks the reading of an existing plan. Kubernetes readiness means each core is a stateless workload behind a contract, with state in the store and coordination through events — not that Kubernetes is required today.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this architectural position observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Explanation

Do not collapse the cores when generating code because it is convenient. The seams are the reason the platform can evolve. When adding capability, add it inside the owning core or propose a new core with an ADR; never let derivation write validation verdicts or let handoff mutate plan objects.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this agent behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Implementation Strategy

Implementation of `Planning Architecture` proceeds in a fixed order so that each step produces evidence the next step can depend on. The order is not a preference; skipping a step produces a core that cannot prove its own correctness.

1. **Model first.** Define the objects, records, and contracts for `Planning Architecture` before writing any behaviour, and register them in the schema registry with a version.
2. **Validate at the boundary.** Reject invalid content at the contract layer so no core downstream has to defend itself against malformed planning content.
3. **Version everything.** Every schema, machine, rule set, and object carries a version, and every change supersedes rather than overwrites.
4. **Observe continuously.** Emit the signals named in this section from the first commit, not after the first incident.
5. **Fail closed.** When a check cannot complete, refuse and record the refusal rather than proceeding on an assumption.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this strategy observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Security

Each core runs with least privilege for its own store namespace and event topics; a compromised derivation core cannot publish a handoff contract because it holds no grant for that topic.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this security property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Performance

The pipeline is designed so the expensive cores (derivation, timeline) are asynchronous and the cheap cores (intake, handoff) are synchronous, keeping interactive latency independent of plan size.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this performance property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Latency

Intake and read paths target interactive latency; derivation and validation are budgeted per plan size class and report progress through events rather than blocking callers.

**Normative application:** For `Planning Architecture`, the owning implementation MUST make this latency property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.
