### Retrieval Purposes and Their Freshness Requirements

Freshness is a property of the purpose, not of the corpus. The same document may be perfectly current for one question and dangerously stale for another, and only the asking side knows which.

| Purpose | Freshness requirement | Item budget | Stale admitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capacity_assumption_lookup` | 90 days | 8 | Yes, with declaration |
| `constraint_precedent` | 365 days | 12 | Yes, with declaration |
| `current_commitment_check` | 1 hour | 20 | No |
| `historic_outcome_review` | No limit | 40 | Not applicable; age is the subject |
| `policy_reference` | Current version only | 6 | No |

`current_commitment_check` is the one to watch. It has a one-hour requirement and admits nothing stale, which means it fails rather than degrades when the corpus is behind. That is correct: a commitment check answered from yesterday's data is worse than no answer, because it will be believed.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this retrieval purpose observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Instruction Shapes Stripped at the Boundary

Stored content that reads as a directive is the mechanism by which a corpus becomes a control plane. These shapes are stripped and counted; the item is excluded and its identity recorded so the source can be corrected.

| Shape | Example pattern | Why it is dangerous |
|---|---|---|
| Imperative addressed to the planner | Directive language naming the system and demanding an action | Executes as a command with no author and no approval |
| Role or persona assignment | Text redefining what the reading system is | Changes behaviour globally from a single stored item |
| Constraint override phrasing | Text asserting that a stated rule does not apply | Attacks the constitution from inside the evidence channel |
| Embedded tool or call syntax | Structured content resembling an invocation | Turns retrieval into execution |
| Output format coercion | Text dictating the shape of the response | Bypasses contract validation by changing the contract |

Stripping is deliberately conservative and will occasionally remove a legitimate item written in an unfortunate style. That cost is acceptable; the alternative is a system whose behaviour can be changed by anyone who can write to the corpus, which in most organisations is a large number of people.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this instruction shape observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Contradiction Handling

When two retrieved items disagree, the retriever's job is to notice and report, not to choose. The choice belongs to the decision, which knows what the answer is for.

| Situation | Retriever action | Decision-side handling |
|---|---|---|
| Same field, different values, both fresh | Cite both, flag the field | Treat as uncertainty; widen the plan's tolerance or escalate |
| Same field, one stale | Cite both with ages | Prefer fresh unless the purpose is historic |
| Different sources, incompatible units | Cite both, flag unit mismatch | Refuse to compare; request normalisation |
| Memory contradicts knowledge base | Cite both, mark the memory as experiential | Experience informs but does not override a current reference |

The last row states an ordering that matters in practice. A remembered outcome is evidence about what happened; a current reference is a statement about what is. When they disagree the reference wins for facts, and the memory becomes a reason to check whether the reference is right.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this contradiction outcome observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operational Stories

Four story types are recorded for `Knowledge and Memory Integration`: a normal-path story, a failure story, a recovery story, and an audit story. Together they describe what this section looks like in operation.

**Normal path.** A planning step declares the `capacity_assumption_lookup` purpose with a ninety-day freshness requirement, receives three items in one hundred and forty-eight milliseconds, cites all three, admits one stale item with an explicit declaration, and surfaces a throughput contradiction to the decision.

**Failure.** A memory note written as an imperative directive addressed to the planner is retrieved. The boundary detects the instruction shape, strips the item, records its identity, and notifies the memory owner. The plan is produced without it, and the note's author is asked to restate it as an observation.

**Recovery.** Investigation shows the note had been retrieved eleven times before stripping was deployed. The citation record lists every plan that cited it, all eleven are reviewed, and two are re-run. Without citation this would have been an investigation; with it, it was a query.

**Audit.** An auditor reconstructs the sequence from the records this section writes, confirming who acted, under which rule set version, with which evidence, and what the outcome was, without asking anyone what happened.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this operational story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Execution Stories

**Execution path.** This section retrieves and cites; it does not decide. Cited evidence enters Section 89's decision context as facts with provenance, and it is Section 89 that weighs contradictions and declares confidence. Nothing retrieved here reaches execution without passing through a decision.

**Boundary note.** The execution story ends at the handoff contract. Planning publishes an execution-ready artefact and stops; the execution surface owns everything after that point and reports back only as events.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this execution story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Optimization Stories

**Optimization path.** Narrowing retrieval from fifty similarity-ranked chunks to eight purpose-scoped items cut context consumption by seventy-one per cent and raised the rate at which planners cited the item that actually determined the outcome from thirty-one per cent to eighty-eight.

**Boundary note.** Optimization changes how well a candidate scores against a declared objective function; it never changes who is authorised to commit. Selection between competing commitments remains a decision and is recorded as one.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this optimization story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Recovery Stories

**Recovery path.** During a knowledge base outage of six minutes, sixty-one plans are produced with declared evidence gaps. They are listed automatically, and when the corpus returns, nine are re-run because their purpose required material that was unavailable. The remaining fifty-two are confirmed as unaffected and closed.

**Boundary note.** Recovery restores a declared state from stored evidence; it never invents state, never edits history in place, and never resumes an action whose authorisation has expired.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this recovery story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

The procedure below is the full constitutional path for `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, from request to evidence. It is the sequence auditors replay.

1. The requesting role submits the action with its inputs, its correlation identifier, and its claimed authority.
2. The contract layer validates structure, references, tenancy, and metadata completeness.
3. The section's guards evaluate in order, each producing a pass or a named refusal reason.
4. On refusal the reason is recorded, the caller is informed, and processing stops with nothing stored.
5. On pass the new version is appended, never updated in place, with a monotonic version number.
6. The receipt named by this section is written and linked to the version digest.
7. A fact is published to the event boundary for consumers that do not need to block.
8. Projections rebuild and publish their lag, making the change visible to grant-holding roles.
9. The action becomes replayable: any auditor can recompute the outcome from stored inputs alone.

### Constitutional Extension

Part 4 extends the planning constitution established in Part 1 Section 3 and continued by Parts 2 and 3, which together contain rules `CAT-PE-CONST-001` through `CAT-PE-CONST-077`. This section contributes exactly one new rule, continuing the catalogue from `CAT-PE-CONST-078` as the Part 3 handoff requires. It adds a final architecture obligation; it does not weaken any existing rule.

**Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-090`  
**Title:** Cited knowledge  
**Normative statement:** Knowledge and memory MUST reach planning only through the retrieval seam; every admitted item MUST be cited with source, version, and timestamp; instruction-shaped content MUST be stripped; freshness MUST be declared per purpose with stale material either excluded or explicitly declared; contradictions MUST be surfaced rather than resolved at retrieval; and write-back MUST be attributed and withdrawable.  
**Rationale:** Memory is the fastest route from a past assumption to a present constraint, and it travels that route silently unless every item carries a date and an author. Citation makes plan reasoning reconstructable and makes poisoned material traceable to every plan it touched. Stripping instruction shapes closes the path by which anyone with write access to a corpus can change system behaviour without an approval.  
**Enforcement point:** Citation is non-optional in the return type, corpus access is restricted to the seam, stripping runs before admission, freshness is enforced per declared purpose, and write-back refuses incomplete attribution.  
**Violation behavior:** The item is excluded and recorded, the plan carries a declared evidence gap, and instruction-shape detections are reported to the source owner as security events.  
**Validation method:** Automated tests covering a directive planted in the corpus, an uncited item, a stale item against a strict purpose, a cross-tenant query, contradictory items, and a write-back without attribution.  
**Owner:** Planning Learning Owner  
**Related Parts 1 to 3 rules:** `CAT-PE-CONST-081` (facts not instructions), `CAT-PE-CONST-083` (disclosed staleness), and `CAT-PE-CONST-091` (deferred choice).

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this constitutional rule observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

#### CAT-PE-P4-88-C17 — Security property upheld

- **Rule:** The security property stated by this section MUST hold in the implementation, not only in the prose.
- **Business test:** The property is stated in the operating contract and is checkable against a running system.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Implementation asserts the property in an automated test and emits the corresponding signal. Property: Retrieval is the widest ingestion surface in the engine and is treated as untrusted input. Material is scoped to a tenant and a purpose, and cross-tenant retrieval is structurally impossible rather than filtered. Instruction-shaped content is stripped at the boundary, which defends against stored prompt injection where an attacker plants a directive in a knowledge item and waits for retrieval. Write-back is attributed and reversible, so a poisoned memory can be identified and withdrawn along with everything that cited it.
- **AI behavior:** The agent MUST NOT trade this property away for throughput or convenience.
- **Human boundary:** Planning Learning Owner approves any deviation, recorded with an expiry.
- **Security assertion:** The property is part of this section's posture and fails closed when unverifiable.
- **Performance assertion:** Verification is bounded by the object under evaluation, not by portfolio size.
- **Evidence:** `knowledge citation record`
- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P4_88_C17`
- **Recovery:** Restore the property, then re-run the section's acceptance tests before resuming.
- **Implementation test:** Automated property test executed in continuous integration.
- **Ownership:** Planning Learning Owner
- **Constitutional assertion:** This control is binding for `Knowledge and Memory Integration` and MUST NOT be weakened without a superseding ADR.

#### CAT-PE-P4-88-C19 — Recovery property upheld

- **Rule:** The recovery property stated by this section MUST hold in the implementation, not only in the prose.
- **Business test:** The property is stated in the operating contract and is checkable against a running system.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Implementation asserts the property in an automated test and emits the corresponding signal. Property: Recovery from a knowledge or memory failure is to resume retrieval and re-run affected planning where the evidence gap was material. Plans produced with declared gaps are listed so that they can be revisited deliberately. Where memory has been poisoned, recovery is withdrawal of the item and re-examination of every plan that cited it, which the citation record makes a query rather than an investigation.
- **AI behavior:** The agent MUST NOT trade this property away for throughput or convenience.
- **Human boundary:** Planning Learning Owner approves any deviation, recorded with an expiry.
- **Security assertion:** The property is part of this section's posture and fails closed when unverifiable.
- **Performance assertion:** Verification is bounded by the object under evaluation, not by portfolio size.

- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P4_88_C19`
- **Recovery:** Restore the property, then re-run the section's acceptance tests before resuming.

- **Ownership:** Planning Learning Owner
- **Constitutional assertion:** This control is binding for `Knowledge and Memory Integration` and MUST NOT be weakened without a superseding ADR.

### Acceptance Tests

The acceptance tests below MUST pass before any implementation of `Knowledge and Memory Integration` is considered complete.

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-001`  
**Purpose:** Direct corpus access is impossible  
**Given:** A planning module attempting a corpus query outside the seam  
**When:** The query is issued  
**Then:** It is refused by policy  
**Failure condition:** Knowledge enters without citation

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-002`  
**Purpose:** Citation is mandatory  
**Given:** A retrieval result missing provenance fields  
**When:** It is admitted to a context  
**Then:** Admission fails  
**Failure condition:** Uncited material enters a plan

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-003`  
**Purpose:** Instruction shapes are stripped  
**Given:** A corpus item containing a directive addressed to the planner  
**When:** It is retrieved  
**Then:** It is stripped, excluded, and recorded  
**Failure condition:** The directive enters the context

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-004`  
**Purpose:** Strict purposes exclude stale material  
**Given:** A `current_commitment_check` and an item two hours old  
**When:** Retrieval runs  
**Then:** The item is excluded  
**Failure condition:** Stale material answers a current-state question

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-005`  
**Purpose:** Stale admission is declared  
**Given:** A tolerant purpose and an item beyond its freshness requirement  
**When:** The item is admitted  
**Then:** A staleness declaration appears in the citation record  
**Failure condition:** Stale material is admitted silently

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-006`  
**Purpose:** Cross-tenant retrieval cannot be expressed  
**Given:** A query attempting another tenant's scope  
**When:** It is issued  
**Then:** It is refused at the corpus  
**Failure condition:** Any foreign item is returned

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-007`  
**Purpose:** Contradictions are surfaced  
**Given:** Two fresh items disagreeing on one field  
**When:** Retrieval completes  
**Then:** Both are cited and the field is flagged  
**Failure condition:** One is dropped or reconciled

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-008`  
**Purpose:** Write-back requires attribution  
**Given:** A memory write with no author or retention period  
**When:** It is attempted  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** An unattributed memory is stored

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-009`  
**Purpose:** Withdrawal traces citing plans  
**Given:** A withdrawn knowledge item  
**When:** The citation record is queried  
**Then:** Every plan that cited it is listed  
**Failure condition:** Affected plans cannot be identified

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-010`  
**Purpose:** Revocation invalidates caches  
**Given:** A cached result containing a withdrawn item  
**When:** Withdrawal occurs  
**Then:** The cache entry is invalidated immediately  
**Failure condition:** The withdrawn item continues to inform plans

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-011`  
**Purpose:** Evidence gaps are declared  
**Given:** An unavailable knowledge system  
**When:** A plan is produced  
**Then:** It carries a declared evidence gap and is listed for revisit  
**Failure condition:** The plan looks fully informed

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S88-012`  
**Purpose:** Caching does not refresh timestamps  
**Given:** A cached item served from a sixty-second cache  
**When:** Its citation is read  
**Then:** The produced-at timestamp is the original  
**Failure condition:** Caching makes material appear newer

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this acceptance test observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Implementation Checklist

This checklist is copied into the implementation task for `Knowledge and Memory Integration` and completed item by item.

- [ ] Retrieval purpose registry with freshness, item, and token budgets.
- [ ] Single retrieval seam with corpus access restricted by policy.
- [ ] Non-optional provenance in the retrieval return type.
- [ ] Instruction-shape detection covering the five declared shapes.
- [ ] Corpus-side tenant scoping with no application filtering path.
- [ ] Contradiction detection with reporting and no resolution logic.
- [ ] Sixty-second scoped cache preserving original timestamps.
- [ ] Immediate cache invalidation on item withdrawal.
- [ ] Attributed, dated, withdrawable memory write-back with retention.
- [ ] Knowledge citation record with retrievals, citations, strippings, and gaps.
- [ ] Object and record schemas for this section registered with a version.
- [ ] Contract-layer validation rejects structurally invalid content.
- [ ] Every reference field resolves at write time or the write is rejected.
- [ ] Every refusal path writes a record with a reason code.
- [ ] Receipts written for every stage in the blueprint.
- [ ] Detection signals emitted for every failure mode listed above.
- [ ] Deny-by-default authorisation enforced at the repository contract layer.
- [ ] Correlation identifier propagated across every stage and every emitted event.
- [ ] Idempotency key honoured on every externally triggered entry point.
- [ ] Timeout and cancellation paths exercised by test, not only by review.
- [ ] Owners and escalation roles resolve in `context/05_AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Proposed repository paths created or explicitly deferred with a record.

### Future Evolution

`Knowledge and Memory Integration` evolves in three directions. First, freshness becomes predictive: the seam learns how quickly each knowledge class actually goes stale and warns when a purpose's declared requirement is optimistic. Second, citation graphs become queryable across plans so that the influence of a single corpus item on downstream decisions can be measured rather than traced by hand. Third, contradiction surfacing becomes proactive, reporting disagreements in the corpus before a retrieval encounters them.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this evolution path observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### 2030 to 2035 Continuities

The following properties of `Knowledge and Memory Integration` are expected to hold through 2035 regardless of implementation technology: role-based ownership, append-only history, evidence-backed completion, deny-by-default access, and a hard boundary against execution. Technologies, languages, and storage engines will change; these five properties are what make planning content written in 2026 still interpretable and still trustworthy in 2035. For knowledge integration specifically, the durable property is that a remembered thing must carry its date and its author wherever it goes. Retrieval architectures, embedding models, and storage engines will be replaced repeatedly; a system whose plans cite dated, attributed evidence will remain explicable under all of them, and one whose planner simply knows things will remain unexplainable under every one.

**Normative application:** For `Knowledge and Memory Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this continuity observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

## 89. Decision Integration

**Section ID:** `CAT-PE-P4-89`  
**Constitutional domain:** Planning decision integration  
**Human accountable owner:** Planning Governance Owner  
**Primary record:** `decision integration record`  
**Decision status:** Final architecture clause set; completes Parts 1 to 3 without weakening them.  
**Primary question:** How does the Planning Engine hand a choice to the Decision Engine, and what may it do while the choice is outstanding?

### Purpose

This section defines the seam between planning and deciding. The Planning Engine produces options, evidence, and consequences; it does not choose between materially different futures. The purpose is to make deferral structural: when a decision is required, planning packages the choice with everything needed to make it, stops at that point, and resumes only when an authorised decision returns. A planner that decides quietly is the single most consequential failure this document exists to prevent.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this purpose observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Scope

This section governs `Decision Integration` for every planning core, contract, record, and interface in the CAT repository. It applies wherever planning content is created, derived, validated, stored, transitioned, read, or retired at runtime. It does not govern execution dispatch, decision authority, or reasoning strategy, which are reached only through declared contracts.

**In scope:** what constitutes a decision point; the decision context contract; option construction and consequence framing; deferral and blocking semantics; decision return, validation, and binding; timeouts and defaults; reversal; and the decision integration record.

**Out of scope:** how decisions are made inside the Decision Engine, which is that document's concern; the human authorities and gates, which are closed in Section 69; execution of a decided plan, which is Section 90; and replanning after a decision changes, which is Section 94.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this boundary observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Business Explanation

Every material planning choice has an owner in the organisation, and the value of this seam is that the owner is named before the choice is made rather than identified after the consequence. Deferral costs time, so the section is equally concerned with keeping the set of decision points small and each package complete: a decision returned in minutes because the context was sufficient is worth more than one avoided entirely by letting the planner guess.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this business outcome observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Engineering Explanation

A decision point is declared, not discovered. Planning detects that a choice is material by the declared criteria, constructs a decision context containing the options, the cited evidence, the consequences of each option, the reversibility of each, and the authority required, then blocks the affected branch. Returned decisions are validated against the context they answer, bound to a version, and recorded. An expired decision request fails the branch; it does not default.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this engineering behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Architecture Explanation

The Decision Engine is an external subsystem reached through one contract. Planning holds the outstanding decision as durable state so a restart does not lose it and does not duplicate it. Because deferral is durable, the seam is asynchronous by default; synchronous decisioning is a latency optimisation over the same contract, never a different path.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this architectural position observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Explanation

An AI participant must recognise a decision point and stop. The characteristic failure is the confident tiebreak: two options are close, the model has a preference, and it proceeds without recording that a choice was made at all. Options must be presented without a recommendation ranking that functions as a decision, consequences must be stated for every option including the null option, and the model must never generate the returned decision itself. Where the model believes one option is clearly better, it says so as evidence with reasoning, and still waits.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this agent behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Implementation Strategy

Implementation of `Decision Integration` proceeds in a fixed order so that each step produces evidence the next step depends on. The order is not a preference; skipping a step produces a core that cannot prove its own correctness.

1. **Model first.** Define the objects, records, and contracts this section names before writing behaviour, and register each in the schema registry with a version.
2. **Validate at the boundary.** Reject invalid content at the contract layer so no downstream core has to defend itself against malformed planning content.
3. **Version everything.** Every schema, machine, rule set, and object carries a version, and every change supersedes rather than overwrites.
4. **Observe continuously.** Emit the signals named in this section from the first commit, not after the first incident.
5. **Fail closed.** When a check cannot complete, refuse and record the refusal rather than proceeding on an assumption.

**Section-specific sequencing.** Declare the decision-point criteria before building the deferral machinery, because a system that can defer but cannot tell when to will either defer everything or nothing, and both are observed in practice.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this strategy observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Implementation Blueprint

An AI assistant implementing `Decision Integration` follows the staged blueprint below. Each stage names what the agent does and the receipt it writes, so a partially completed implementation can be resumed by a different agent without re-reading the whole part.

| Stage | Name | What the agent does | Receipt written |
|---|---|---|---|
| `classify` | Classify materiality | Applies the declared criteria to determine whether a choice is a decision point. | `classify` stage receipt |
| `enumerate` | Enumerate options | Constructs the option set including the null option. | `enumerate` stage receipt |
| `evidence` | Attach evidence | Attaches cited evidence from Section 88 with freshness and contradictions. | `evidence` stage receipt |

| `validate` | Validate return | Checks the decision against the context version, option set, and authority. | `validate` stage receipt |
| `bind` | Bind | Binds the chosen option into the plan with its decision reference. | `bind` stage receipt |
| `record` | Write record | Writes the decision integration record with contexts, returns, and timings. | `record` stage receipt |

### AI Failure Library

These are the failures agents actually produce when implementing `Decision Integration`. Each entry names the mistake, the reason an agent makes it, and the corrective behaviour.

| Failure | Why an agent does it | Corrective behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Choosing between close options without recording a decision | The difference seemed immaterial | Materiality is determined by declared criteria, not by perceived closeness |
| Ranking options so strongly that the choice is made in the framing | The recommendation was meant to help | Present consequences per option; reasoning is evidence, not a ranking that decides |
| Defaulting when a decision request expires | Progress seemed better than stalling | Expiry fails the branch; there is no default option |
| Omitting the null option | Doing nothing was not considered viable | The null option is always present with its consequences stated |
| Inventing a field the schema does not define | The agent needs somewhere to put a value and adds a field rather than asking | Propose a schema change with a version bump; never write undeclared fields |
| Weakening a guard to make a test pass | The guard blocks the happy path the agent is building | Fix the input or the design; a weakened guard is a silent constitutional violation |
| Treating a planned document as if it exists | Cross-references look uniform | Check status; planned documents are cited with `Status: Planned` |

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this failure mode observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Optimization

Optimising agent work on `Decision Integration` means making each decision package complete on the first attempt, because the dominant cost of deferral is not the wait but the round trip when a decider asks for information that should have been included. It also means batching related decision points into one context where they share evidence, which reduces both decider effort and the risk of inconsistent answers.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this optimisation observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Developer Notes

Engineers should persist the outstanding decision before returning from the deferral call. A decision request held only in memory is lost on restart, and the branch either hangs forever or, worse, resumes without it after a redeploy that nobody connected to the missing decision.

### Security

Returned decisions are authenticated and their authority verified against the requirement stated in the context. A decision bound to a context version cannot be replayed against a different version, which prevents an old approval from authorising a changed plan. The engine never generates a decision, and a returned decision whose source is an automated participant is refused for any context requiring a human authority. Decision records are append-only and signed, because they are the primary evidence of who chose what.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this security property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Performance

Constructing a decision context is bounded work: option enumeration is capped, evidence is already cited from retrieval, and consequence framing is computed from the same models planning already uses. Blocking is free — the branch consumes no resources while deferred — which is what makes deferral affordable enough to use whenever the criteria say it is required.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this performance property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Latency

Context construction completes within five hundred milliseconds. The waiting time is a human or external property and is measured but not bounded by the engine; what the engine bounds is the request deadline, after which the branch fails. Binding a returned decision and resuming the branch completes within one second.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this latency property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Scalability

Outstanding decisions are durable rows, so tens of thousands may be open simultaneously without consuming runtime capacity. The scaling limit is decider attention, not system capacity, which is why the criteria that create decision points are governed and reviewed rather than left to each planning module.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this scalability property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Reliability and Availability

A deferred branch survives restart, failover, and redeploy because the outstanding decision is durable state with a correlation identifier. If the Decision Engine is unavailable, decision contexts queue and their deadlines continue to run; the engine does not proceed and does not silently extend deadlines, because both would convert an availability problem into an unrecorded decision.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this reliability property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Caching

Decision contexts are not cached; each is constructed for a specific plan version. What is cached is the evidence underlying them, through Section 88's retrieval cache. Returned decisions are cached against their context version so that a duplicate return is recognised as idempotent rather than treated as a second decision.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this caching property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Consistency

A decision is bound to exactly one plan version. If the plan changes materially while a decision is outstanding, the outstanding request is invalidated and reissued against the new version rather than answered against the old, because the option set and consequences the decider saw no longer describe the situation.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this consistency property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Recovery Strategy

Recovery from a failure while decisions are outstanding is to reload durable decision state and reconcile: requests whose deadlines passed during the outage fail their branches explicitly, and requests still within deadline continue. Where a decision was returned but not bound, the idempotency key allows the binding to complete without creating a second decision.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this recovery property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Monitoring and Observability

Observability for `Decision Integration` is defined by its failure modes: every failure mode has a detection signal, and every detection signal is emitted by the implementation rather than inferred by an operator. A failure mode with no signal is an unmonitored failure mode and is treated as a gap.

- **Counters:** decision points raised, contexts constructed, decisions returned, decisions refused on authority, decisions refused on version mismatch, requests expired, branches failed on expiry, decisions reversed, contexts invalidated by plan change.
- **Gauges:** outstanding decisions by authority, oldest outstanding decision age, branches currently blocked, contexts awaiting evidence, decisions approaching deadline.
- **Histograms:** context construction time, time to decision return, options per context, evidence items per context, time from return to binding.
- **Traces:** one span per blueprint stage, correlated by plan identity and correlation identifier.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this signal observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Runtime Behaviour

At runtime planning reaches a point the criteria mark as material. It enumerates options including the null option, attaches cited evidence with any contradictions surfaced from Section 88, frames consequences per option, names the required authority, persists the context, and blocks the branch. Other branches continue. When a decision returns, the engine verifies the authority, verifies the context version, verifies the chosen option is in the offered set, binds the choice with its decision reference, and resumes. If the deadline passes first, the branch fails with an explicit reason that names the unanswered decision, and no option is selected.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this runtime behaviour observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Maintainability

Maintainability of `Decision Integration` depends on keeping declarations declarative: schemas, machines, rules, and grants are data, compiled and validated at startup, so a change is reviewed as a diff of intent rather than a diff of conditionals scattered across services. Every declaration is versioned, and a version is retired only when no live object is pinned to it. For this seam specifically, maintainability means the materiality criteria live in one governed document rather than as conditionals scattered through planning modules. Every team that adds a conditional adds a decision point nobody reviewed, and the set drifts until it either blocks everything or nothing.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this maintainability property observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

| Outstanding decision lost on restart | Blocked branches resuming without a decision after a redeploy | Durable persistence before the deferral call returns | Planning Platform Owner |
| Decision point proliferation | Rising deferral rate with falling decider response rate | Criteria governed centrally and reviewed quarterly | Planning Contract Owner |
| Duplicate decision on retry | Two bindings for one context | Idempotency key on the context; the second return is recognised | Planning Coordination Owner |

### Extension Points

`Decision Integration` is extended by adding declarations, never by editing behaviour in place. A new decision point is added by declaring its materiality criterion, its required authority, its deadline, and its context template, and by having governance review the addition. A criterion may be tightened without review; loosening one, which reduces the number of decisions requiring an authority, requires the same review as adding a new authority path. Any extension that changes an existing declaration's meaning is a superseding version, not an extension.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this extension point observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Risks

| Risk | Impact if unmanaged | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Materiality criteria defined per module | The decision set drifts and nobody can state what requires a decision | One governed criteria document, reviewed quarterly |
| Deferral without durability | Restarts silently drop or duplicate decisions | Persist the context before the deferral call returns; idempotency at binding |
| Deadlines extended during outages | An availability failure becomes an unrecorded decision | Deadlines run regardless; expiry fails the branch explicitly |
| Recommendation framing that decides | The decider ratifies rather than chooses and accountability is fictional | Consequences per option, reasoning as evidence, no ranking presented as a choice |

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this risk observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Anti-patterns

- **Treating a timeout as an approval.** The most consequential decisions are the ones nobody answered.
- **Presenting a single option with alternatives 'for completeness'.** It is a decision already made, wearing the costume of a choice.
- **Blocking the entire plan on one decision.** Unrelated branches stall and teams learn to avoid raising decision points.
- **Storing decisions only in the plan record.** The decision cannot be audited independently of the thing it authorised.
- **Letting the planner choose the required authority.** The authority set is closed in Section 69 and mapping to it is a governed rule.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this prohibition observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Best Practices

- Declare materiality criteria centrally and review them on a schedule.
- Always include the null option with its consequences.
- Persist the decision context before blocking.
- Bind decisions to a context version and reject mismatches.
- Block only the affected branch, never the whole plan.
- Fail on expiry; never default.
- Record decisions append-only and independently of the plan.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this practice observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Counter Examples

A team ships a planner that raises decisions by writing to a chat channel and proceeds after fifteen minutes with its preferred option if nobody replies. It works for a quarter. Then a four-hundred-thousand-unit reallocation happens at two in the morning, the fifteen minutes elapse, and the resulting audit question — who approved this — has no answer.

The following configuration is rejected by the guards described in this section:

```json
{
  "object": "rejected_decision_integration_configuration",
  "section": "CAT-PE-P4-89",
  "submitted": {
    "materiality_criteria": "per_module_conditionals",
    "decision_channel": "chat_notification",
    "on_timeout": "proceed_with_engine_preference",
    "options_presented": "preferred_option_only",
    "null_option": "omitted",
    "authority_verification": null,
    "context_versioning": null,
    "persistence": "in_memory",
    "decision_record": "embedded_in_plan_only"
  },
  "errors": []
}
```

- **Rejected:** Per-module criteria mean nobody can state what requires a decision.
- **Rejected:** A chat notification is not an authenticated decision channel.
- **Rejected:** Proceeding on timeout makes silence an approval.
- **Rejected:** A single presented option is a decision already made.
- **Rejected:** Omitting the null option hides the cost of doing nothing.
- **Rejected:** Without authority verification, anyone who can reply can decide.
- **Rejected:** Without context versioning, an approval survives the plan it approved.
- **Rejected:** In-memory deferral loses decisions on every restart.
- **Rejected:** A decision recorded only in the plan cannot be audited independently.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this rejection observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Pseudo Code

The logic below is complete for the behaviour it describes; it contains no omission markers and can be transliterated into any of the languages named in Section 5.

```text
CRITERIA = load_governed_materiality_criteria()    # one document, reviewed quarterly
AUTHORITIES = SECTION_69_CLOSED_AUTHORITY_SET

function evaluate_choice(plan, branch, choice):
    crit = CRITERIA.match(choice)
    if crit is absent:
        return proceed(choice.only_option)             # not material by declared criteria

    ctx = build_context(plan, branch, choice, crit)
    require(ctx.options contains NULL_OPTION)
    require(every option has consequence, cost, reversibility, commitments_affected)
    require(ctx.authority_required in AUTHORITIES)
    require(ctx.evidence is cited via section 88)

    persist(ctx)                                       # durable BEFORE blocking
    block_branch(branch, awaiting=ctx.id, deadline=crit.deadline)
    return DEFERRED                                    # other branches continue

function on_decision_returned(decision):
    ctx = load(decision.context_id)
    if ctx is absent:                        return refuse("unknown_context")
    if ctx.bound:                            return acknowledge_idempotent(ctx)
    if decision.context_version != ctx.version:
                                             return refuse("context_version_mismatch")
    if decision.chosen_option not in ctx.options:
                                             return refuse("option_not_in_offered_set")
    if not authority_of(decision.actor) satisfies ctx.authority_required:
                                             return refuse_security("authority_insufficient")
    if ctx.authority_required.requires_human and decision.source_type != "human":
                                             return refuse_security("automated_source")

    bind(ctx, decision)                                # append-only, signed
    resume_branch(ctx.branch, with_option=decision.chosen_option)

function on_deadline(ctx):
    if ctx.bound: return
    fail_branch(ctx.branch, reason="decision_not_returned", context=ctx.id)
    # no default option is selected, ever

function on_plan_changed(plan, ctx):
    if materially_changes(ctx.options, ctx.consequences, plan):
        invalidate(ctx, reason="plan_version_advanced")
        reissue_against(plan.version)                  # the decider sees the current situation
```

### Materiality Criteria

A choice becomes a decision point when it meets a declared criterion. The set is governed centrally so that the question 'what requires a decision here' has one answer that a person can read.

| Criterion | Threshold | Authority required | Deadline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commitment impact | More than 3 commitments or 250,000 units | Planning commitment authority | 8 working hours |
| Irreversibility | Any option whose reversal cost is contractual | Planning commitment authority | 24 hours |
| Cost threshold | Delta above the tenant's declared limit | Financial authority | 24 hours |
| Policy boundary | Any option touching a policy envelope | Governance authority | 48 hours |
| Safety or compliance | Any option affecting a regulated obligation | Compliance authority | 4 hours |
| Cross-tenant effect | Any option affecting another tenant | Governance authority | 24 hours |

Tightening a threshold is an ordinary change; loosening one is a governance review, because loosening removes decisions from human hands and that is the direction in which this system fails.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this materiality criterion observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### What a Complete Decision Context Contains

The completeness checklist exists because the dominant cost of deferral is the round trip. A context missing any of these elements is refused at construction rather than sent and returned.

| Element | Requirement | Why it is mandatory |
|---|---|---|
| Option set | At least two, including the null option | A single option is not a choice |
| Per-option consequence | Stated for every option | Comparison is impossible without it |
| Per-option reversibility | Stated with reversal cost | Reversibility usually dominates the choice |
| Cited evidence | Provenance and freshness from Section 88 | The decider must be able to check the basis |
| Surfaced contradictions | Any disagreement in the evidence | Hidden disagreement produces false confidence |
| Commitments affected | Counted per option | Connects the choice to the obligations it touches |
| Required authority | One value from the closed set | Names the accountable party before the choice |
| Deadline | Absolute time with a stated expiry consequence | Makes the cost of not deciding explicit |

Note what is absent: a recommendation field that selects an option. Reasoning is included as evidence and is often decisive in practice, but it is presented as argument rather than as a default that the decider merely confirms.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this context element observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Deferral Outcomes

Four outcomes are possible for an outstanding decision, and each has a defined effect on the plan. None of them is 'the engine proceeded'.

| Outcome | Effect on the branch | Effect on the plan | Recorded as |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decision returned and valid | Resumes with the chosen option | Plan advances with a decision reference | Bound decision |
| Deadline passed | Fails with an explicit reason | Plan is incomplete and marked | Expired decision |
| Plan changed materially | Remains blocked, context reissued | New context at the current version | Invalidated context |
| Decision reversed after binding | Replanning triggered | Section 94 produces a revised plan | Reversal with reason |

Reversal is deliberately supported. A decision made with the best available evidence can still be wrong, and a system where reversal is impossible pushes deciders toward delay, which is the more expensive failure.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this deferral outcome observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operational Stories

Four story types are recorded for `Decision Integration`: a normal-path story, a failure story, a recovery story, and an audit story. Together they describe what this section looks like in operation.

**Normal path.** A supply reallocation meets the commitment-impact criterion. The engine constructs a three-option context in four hundred and twelve milliseconds, blocks one branch, and resumes eighty-three minutes later when a named authority selects the reversible switch-to-line-B option, which binds in under a second.

**Failure.** A compliance-criterion decision with a four-hour deadline is not answered overnight. At expiry the branch fails with `decision_not_returned`, naming the context. No option is selected, the plan is marked incomplete, and the morning shift sees an explicit unanswered decision rather than a silently chosen path.

**Recovery.** The unanswered decision is escalated to the compliance authority's deputy, answered, and the branch is replanned from the failure point. Total delay is eleven hours. The alternative — a default selection at two in the morning — would have been faster and unattributable.

**Audit.** An auditor reconstructs the sequence from the records this section writes, confirming who acted, under which rule set version, with which evidence, and what the outcome was, without asking anyone what happened.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this operational story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Execution Stories

**Execution path.** This section decides nothing. It packages choices, blocks, validates returns, and binds. The Decision Engine chooses, Section 69's authorities are accountable, and Section 90 executes what was bound. A plan that reaches execution without a decision reference at a declared decision point is rejected there, which is the second line of defence.

**Boundary note.** The execution story ends at the handoff contract. Planning publishes an execution-ready artefact and stops; the execution surface owns everything after that point and reports back only as events.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this execution story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Optimization Stories

**Optimization path.** Batching related decision points that shared evidence reduced contexts raised per month from two thousand four hundred to one thousand eight hundred and eighty-two, and cut the rate of contexts returned for more information from six per cent to two.

**Boundary note.** Optimization changes how well a candidate scores against a declared objective function; it never changes who is authorised to commit. Selection between competing commitments remains a decision and is recorded as one.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this optimization story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Recovery Stories

**Recovery path.** A cluster restart occurs with two hundred and eleven outstanding decisions. All are reloaded from durable state. Fourteen had passed their deadlines during the outage and their branches fail explicitly; one had been returned but not bound, and the idempotency key allows the binding to complete without creating a second decision.

**Boundary note.** Recovery restores a declared state from stored evidence; it never invents state, never edits history in place, and never resumes an action whose authorisation has expired.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this recovery story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operating Contract

The operating contract for `Decision Integration` is the short form of everything above, and it is what an on-call engineer reads at three in the morning.

| Clause | Commitment |
|---|---|
| Guarantee | Every accepted write satisfies the controls in this section and produces a receipt. |
| Refusal | Every refusal names a reason code and is recorded; nothing partial is stored. |
| Owner | Planning Governance Owner |
| Evidence | `decision integration record` |
| Escalation | Section owner, then the Planning Owner Council, then the Lead Repository Architect. |
| Degradation | Fail closed: refuse and record rather than proceed on an assumption. |
| Budget | Stated in the performance and latency blocks above; exceeding a budget is a signal, not an exception. |

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this contractual commitment observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

The procedure below is the full constitutional path for `Decision Integration`, from request to evidence. It is the sequence auditors replay.

1. The requesting role submits the action with its inputs, its correlation identifier, and its claimed authority.
2. The contract layer validates structure, references, tenancy, and metadata completeness.
3. The section's guards evaluate in order, each producing a pass or a named refusal reason.
4. On refusal the reason is recorded, the caller is informed, and processing stops with nothing stored.
5. On pass the new version is appended, never updated in place, with a monotonic version number.
6. The receipt named by this section is written and linked to the version digest.
7. A fact is published to the event boundary for consumers that do not need to block.
8. Projections rebuild and publish their lag, making the change visible to grant-holding roles.
9. The action becomes replayable: any auditor can recompute the outcome from stored inputs alone.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this procedural step observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Required Decision Record

Any change to `Decision Integration` requires a decision record containing the following fields. A change proposed without them is returned unreviewed.

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Decision ID | A new ADR identifier in `adr/` |
| Superseded clause | The exact control or requirement identifier being changed |
| Rationale | Why the current behaviour is insufficient, with evidence |
| Impact | Which cores, records, and grants change as a result |
| Migration | How existing objects pinned to the current version are handled |
| Approver | Planning Governance Owner plus the Lead Repository Architect |
| Validation | How the new behaviour will be tested before it takes effect |

### Constitutional Extension

Part 4 extends the planning constitution established in Part 1 Section 3 and continued by Parts 2 and 3, which together contain rules `CAT-PE-CONST-001` through `CAT-PE-CONST-077`. This section contributes exactly one new rule, continuing the catalogue from `CAT-PE-CONST-078` as the Part 3 handoff requires. It adds a final architecture obligation; it does not weaken any existing rule.

**Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-091`  
**Title:** Deferred choice  
**Normative statement:** Where a choice meets a governed materiality criterion, the Planning Engine MUST construct a complete decision context including the null option, persist it, block only the affected branch, and resume only on a decision that is authenticated, authority-verified, and bound to the answered context version; expiry MUST fail the branch and MUST NOT select an option.  
**Rationale:** The failure this prevents is not a wrong choice but an unattributed one. A planner that resolves material choices silently produces outcomes nobody chose, and the absence is discovered only when the outcome is questioned, by which time the reasoning is unrecoverable. Blocking one branch rather than the plan keeps deferral cheap enough that teams do not route around it.  
**Enforcement point:** Criteria are centrally governed, contexts are refused when incomplete, deferral persists before blocking, binding verifies authority and version, and the expiry path contains no selection logic.  
**Violation behavior:** The branch fails with an explicit unanswered-decision reason, or the return is refused and, where authority or source was wrong, recorded as a security event.  
**Validation method:** Automated tests covering a silent tiebreak attempt, an expired deadline, a replayed approval against a new plan version, an agent answering a human authority, a restart with outstanding decisions, and a duplicate return.  
**Owner:** Planning Governance Owner  
**Related Parts 1 to 3 rules:** `CAT-PE-CONST-082` (authorised intent only), `CAT-PE-CONST-096` (bounded autonomy), and `CAT-PE-CONST-069` (human oversight gates).

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this constitutional rule observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

#### CAT-PE-P4-89-C09 — Contain: Silent tiebreak

- **Rule:** When `silent tiebreak` is detected, the containment action MUST be binding required before a branch may pass a declared decision point
- **Business test:** The organisation learns about this failure from a signal rather than from a customer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Detection signal: Plan branch progressing past a material choice with no decision reference. Containment is executed by the owning core, not by an operator following a runbook from memory.
- **AI behavior:** The agent MUST NOT suppress, retry past, or reinterpret this condition; it reports and stops.
- **Human boundary:** Planning Governance Owner is accountable for the containment action and its record.
- **Security assertion:** An uncontained failure of this kind leaves the system in a state whose authorisation properties are unknown.
- **Performance assertion:** Detection is continuous and adds a bounded per-operation cost; containment is bounded by the affected object set.
- **Evidence:** `decision integration record`
- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P4_89_C09`
- **Recovery:** Execute the containment action, write the recovery receipt, then re-run the section's acceptance tests before resuming.
- **Implementation test:** Failure injection test triggering the condition and asserting the declared containment, not merely the absence of a crash.
- **Ownership:** Planning Governance Owner
- **Constitutional assertion:** This control is binding for `Decision Integration` and MUST NOT be weakened without a superseding ADR.

#### CAT-PE-P4-89-C17 — Security property upheld

- **Rule:** The security property stated by this section MUST hold in the implementation, not only in the prose.
- **Business test:** The property is stated in the operating contract and is checkable against a running system.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Implementation asserts the property in an automated test and emits the corresponding signal. Property: Returned decisions are authenticated and their authority verified against the requirement stated in the context. A decision bound to a context version cannot be replayed against a different version, which prevents an old approval from authorising a changed plan. The engine never generates a decision, and a returned decision whose source is an automated participant is refused for any context requiring a human authority. Decision records are append-only and signed, because they are the primary evidence of who chose what.
- **AI behavior:** The agent MUST NOT trade this property away for throughput or convenience.
- **Human boundary:** Planning Governance Owner approves any deviation, recorded with an expiry.
- **Security assertion:** The property is part of this section's posture and fails closed when unverifiable.
- **Performance assertion:** Verification is bounded by the object under evaluation, not by portfolio size.
- **Evidence:** `decision integration record`
- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P4_89_C17`
- **Recovery:** Restore the property, then re-run the section's acceptance tests before resuming.
- **Implementation test:** Automated property test executed in continuous integration.
- **Ownership:** Planning Governance Owner
- **Constitutional assertion:** This control is binding for `Decision Integration` and MUST NOT be weakened without a superseding ADR.

### Acceptance Tests

The acceptance tests below MUST pass before any implementation of `Decision Integration` is considered complete.

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-001`  
**Purpose:** Material choices cannot be resolved internally  
**Given:** A choice meeting a governed criterion  
**When:** Planning attempts to proceed without a decision  
**Then:** The branch is blocked  
**Failure condition:** The plan advances with no decision reference

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-002`  
**Purpose:** Null option is always present  
**Given:** Any constructed decision context  
**When:** Its option set is read  
**Then:** The null option is present with consequences  
**Failure condition:** Doing nothing is not offered

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-003`  
**Purpose:** Incomplete contexts are refused  
**Given:** A context missing per-option reversibility  
**When:** Construction completes  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** An incomplete context is sent to a decider

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-004`  
**Purpose:** Deferral is durable  
**Given:** Outstanding decisions and a process restart  
**When:** The engine recovers  
**Then:** All outstanding decisions are reloaded  
**Failure condition:** A blocked branch resumes or is lost

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-005`  
**Purpose:** Expiry fails the branch  
**Given:** A decision deadline passing unanswered  
**When:** The deadline handler runs  
**Then:** The branch fails and no option is selected  
**Failure condition:** Any option is chosen by default

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-006`  
**Purpose:** Version mismatch is refused  
**Given:** A decision answering context version 6 against version 7  
**When:** Binding is attempted  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** A stale approval binds to a changed plan

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-007`  
**Purpose:** Authority is verified  
**Given:** A return from an actor lacking the required authority  
**When:** Binding is attempted  
**Then:** It is refused and recorded as a security event  
**Failure condition:** The decision binds

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-008`  
**Purpose:** Agents cannot answer human authorities  
**Given:** A human-authority context and an automated source  
**When:** The return is processed  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** An agent decides a human decision

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-009`  
**Purpose:** Option must be in the offered set  
**Given:** A returned option not present in the context  
**When:** Binding is attempted  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** An unoffered option is bound

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-010`  
**Purpose:** Duplicate returns are idempotent  
**Given:** A decision returned twice with the same idempotency key  
**When:** Both are processed  
**Then:** One binding exists  
**Failure condition:** Two decisions are recorded

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-011`  
**Purpose:** Plan change invalidates the context  
**Given:** A material plan change while a decision is outstanding  
**When:** The change is applied  
**Then:** The context is invalidated and reissued at the new version  
**Failure condition:** The decider answers a situation that no longer exists

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S89-012`  
**Purpose:** Only the affected branch blocks  
**Given:** A plan with three independent branches and one decision point  
**When:** Deferral occurs  
**Then:** The other two branches continue  
**Failure condition:** The whole plan stalls

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this acceptance test observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Memory Anchor

An agent that retains nothing else from this section retains the following. A seam that packages material choices with options, evidence, consequences, and a named authority, blocks the affected branch, and binds only authenticated, version-matched decisions. The engine never chooses, expiry never defaults, and no branch passes a declared decision point without a binding.

**Memory anchor ID:** `CAT-PE-MEM-S89-001`  
**Concept:** A seam that packages material choices with options, evidence, consequences, and a named authority, blocks the affected branch, and binds only authenticated, version-matched decisions.  
**Invariant:** The engine never chooses, expiry never defaults, and no branch passes a declared decision point without a binding.  
**Relationship:** This section consumes Section 88's cited evidence, respects Section 69's authorities, and feeds Section 90's execution.  
**Implementation implication:** Implementations MUST persist before blocking and MUST keep the expiry path free of any selection logic.

**Anchor:** `Decision Integration` = package the choice, block the branch, never decide, governed by Planning decision integration, evidenced by `decision integration record`, owned by Planning Governance Owner.

### Future Evolution

`Decision Integration` evolves in three directions. First, decision contexts acquire simulated outcomes per option so that consequences are demonstrated rather than described. Second, deferral becomes anticipatory: the engine raises a likely decision point before the branch reaches it, so the waiting happens in parallel with work rather than in series. Third, criteria calibration becomes evidence-driven, using outcome data to identify thresholds that raise decisions nobody needed and, more importantly, choices that should have been decisions and were not.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this evolution path observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### 2030 to 2035 Continuities

The following properties of `Decision Integration` are expected to hold through 2035 regardless of implementation technology: role-based ownership, append-only history, evidence-backed completion, deny-by-default access, and a hard boundary against execution. Technologies, languages, and storage engines will change; these five properties are what make planning content written in 2026 still interpretable and still trustworthy in 2035. For this seam specifically, the durable property is that a material choice must have a named chooser recorded before its consequence occurs. Decision-support technology, automation levels, and organisational structures will all change; a system that can always answer who chose this and on what basis will remain accountable under any of them, and one that cannot will fail its first serious review regardless of how well it plans.

**Normative application:** For `Decision Integration`, the owning implementation MUST make this continuity observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.
